### Form defaults and retention — approved product direction

Latest user direction: offer familiar forms, keep responses private to the team managing them, allow direct staff corrections, and avoid a specialized compliance workflow. No respondent edits or uploads. These contracts do not claim implemented behavior or legal certification.

- **Collection:** authors choose ordinary form questions and validation using the P4 field menu. Do not add an ID/medical/payment classification flow, extra policy questionnaire or model-based content screening as a prerequisite. No respondent file-upload control. Basic input validation, private access and safe rendering remain required.
- **Audience:** the form manager selects public or invited/signed-in respondents. Submission never grants access to other responses. **[ANSWERED]** Form creators/managers/editors can see incoming responses without separate reviewer setup; responses remain private to authorized form collaborators. Publishing a form does not publish its dataset.
- **Notice:** show collecting organization, purpose, storage destination, retention period and a contact before submission. No unrelated reuse or AI processing outside the authorized task and processing policy.
- **Retention — [ANSWERED D4]:** no default 12-month deletion. Keep canonical responses until an authorized organization manager deletes them, with an annual review reminder rather than an expiration date. An organization keeping useful records for four years should not lose them merely because they are old. An optional explicit per-form deletion period may override the organization default when permitted by its policy. This is approved product behavior; it does not override an organization's applicable retention obligations or published notice. Explicit organization closure uses the 30-day window in P4; provider lifecycle, backup/history retention and transient cleanup require technical qualification; do not confuse them with live record retention.
- **Optional timed-deletion enforcement:** store the scoped policy/version, retention anchor and duration; derive eligibility from the chosen event (initially submission time), not login/activity. A bounded scheduled server job must recheck current policy, record identity, access/holds if supported, and concurrent changes before each effect; record idempotent deletion receipts. Show affected counts and warn before a policy change makes existing records eligible. Any recovery/trash window is additional retained time and must be disclosed separately from final purge. Do not expose an automatic-deletion toggle until the selected destination supports and proves it. The manual-retention MVP does not require a universal retention engine.
- **Google and backups:** a Google adapter may remove only our identified responses with explicit authority, never unrelated rows/the whole Sheet. Lost authority produces a blocked/pending result, not success. Provider history, backups, exports and independently downloaded copies are distinct; do not promise immediate erasure everywhere. P5 excludes durable local answer buffers for Google delivery; canonical response retention remains separate from minimal receipt retention.

**Reference check, October 29:** [Tally](https://tally.so/help/submissions-data-retention) makes timed response deletion optional, permits periods from minutes to years and retains incoming submissions indefinitely when disabled; deleted submissions have a separate 90-day trash period. [Google Vault](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/vault/retention/retain-drive-files-with-vault) supports fixed or indefinite file retention. Vault file policies are not a per-response Sheets deletion adapter. [Airtable](https://support.airtable.com/articles/3982973603-creating-and-managing-data-retention-policies-in-airtable) separates revision/snapshot retention, trash and configurable inactive-base deletion. These examples support separating policy types; they do not establish Coach House implementation or regulatory sufficiency.
- **Corrections:** no respondent editing or edit links. The receipt names an organization contact. Authorized form creators/managers/editors can correct submitted answer cells directly, such as a misspelled name or email. Record who changed which fields and when; enforce revisions without requiring a correction-note workflow. Do not change the published question/version meaning. Google corrections write to Google and surface source changes truthfully.
- **Recovery and audit:** keep minimal access/change/delivery receipts without raw answers in logs. Google response bodies are processed only in flight for immediate delivery; do not retain them in a durable buffer or background delivery queue. Minimal identity/outcome records support reconciliation without storing answers, as defined in P5. Apply the same retention intent to controlled caches/exports; never promise deletion of recipients' copies.

Revocation denies subsequent authorized reads/writes and invalidates controlled caches, subscriptions and asset grants as applicable. It cannot recall content already downloaded or copied by a recipient. Do not expose connected private records or persist signed private URLs publicly. Preserve failed/offline input without promising conflict-free offline editing.

### P4. Simple form authoring, team responses and closure

**[ANSWERED; latest user direction supersedes earlier reviewer/annotation proposals]** The normal flow is **create questions → share → see responses → edit cells**. Reuse and extend the existing builder; do not rebuild a form platform or add a privacy wizard. Match the supplied familiar question-card interaction using Coach House components, not copied branding. The screenshots define behavior and the target type menu, not proof of current implementation.

#### Form field and interaction contract

| Target control | Typed answer / behavior | Existing versus required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Short answer / Paragraph | Bounded string; optional supported validation; paragraph is multiline | Existing short/long answer; preserve existing email/number types and saved values, expose their validation naturally without breaking storage |
| Multiple choice / Dropdown | One stable option ID; dropdown is a compact presentation | Existing single choice; dropdown implemented locally in S08 November1. Single-choice Other implemented locally in S08 November1, with a separate bounded text value; dropdown stays ordinary choice |
| Checkboxes | Unique set of stable option IDs; optional Other text | Other implemented locally in S08 November1; reserved version/question-scoped identity plus separate bounded text, never label-based identity |
| Linear scale / Rating | Integer within configured bounds; endpoints/scale labels or accessible rating symbols | Linear scale and rating implemented locally in S08 November1; shared typed controls/validation, keyboard and numeric alternatives. Hosted/release qualification remains |
| Multiple choice grid | Stable row IDs mapped to one column option ID per answered row | Implemented locally in S08 November1: version-bound membership/required rows; mobile stacked controls; up to20 rows and10 columns. Hosted/release qualification remains |
| Checkbox grid | Stable row IDs mapped to sets of column option IDs | Implemented locally in S08 November1: unique permitted column IDs and required rows; same bounded axes/mobile controls; public answers and staff corrections |
| Date / Time | Valid local calendar date or local time, not an implicitly converted UTC instant | Native pickers and timezone-free validation implemented locally in S08 November1; a distinct scheduled-event contract may separately request a timezone |

Question cards support inline title/options, type selection, Required, duplicate, delete and drag/keyboard reorder. Keep ordinary controls visible and secondary settings in one small menu. Type changes preserve compatible values; incompatible options or published response mappings require an explicit change, never silent data loss. Published versions keep stable question/option/row/column identities; adding or changing a draft does not reinterpret older responses. Duplication generates new identities. No respondent file upload, scoring, conditional workflow engine or payment integration is implied. Author-added decorative images are separate from respondent uploads and may reuse qualified assets without blocking basic form delivery.

**AI and external forms:** AI can draft the same typed form definition a person edits, or suggest using an existing/new Google Form when that is simpler or already fits the organization's workflow. Represent an external form as a useful link/step on the plan. Do not require rebuilding it in Coach House. A linked Google Form is not the same feature as a Coach House form writing to Google Sheets. Do not claim automatic external-form creation, editing, embedding or response sync without a real qualified integration; link-out is sufficient for the suggestion. Native basic forms remain in scope; this option does not silently remove them.

#### Team access and direct corrections

Creating a form grants its creator form management; authorized form editors/managers can view incoming responses and edit answer cells. Make this meaning clear in the existing sharing control; no second mandatory reviewer list or publication setup. View-only plan/public access does not grant private response access. A manager can grant scoped read-only response review when needed. Source restrictions still apply: connecting a Sheet does not give teammates the connector owner's credentials or Google permissions. If the source blocks access, show that boundary and the existing access/connect action rather than silently broadening it.

Correct cells through the canonical response writer with stable response identity, validation, current revision and independent readback. Record actor/time/changed-field identifiers; do not turn this into a mandatory annotation or approval workflow. Technical submission ID, timestamps and published-version linkage are not editable answer cells. Keep a user's unsaved edit when another edit conflicts. For Google, update the canonical cells and do not retain answer copies in platform logs/history. A submission retry must return its existing receipt and never restore the pre-correction answers. Respondents still cannot edit after submission. Export/deletion/sharing remain separately authorized actions within the existing permission system.

**Notice:** use a concise pre-submit organization/contact, destination and actual retention explanation; disclose enabled AI processing where relevant. No new blanket checkbox or sensitive-data questionnaire. Public sharing never includes the response table automatically.

#### Explicit organization closure

**[ANSWERED: 30 days]** Organization owner requests closure; stop public intake/publication and new AI work immediately. Allow a **30-day restricted export/cancel window**, then purge Coach House-controlled organization content. Export still requires each dataset's authority: closure does not broaden response access. An owner may request earlier permanent deletion with explicit consequences. Canceling a subscription, a payment failure, removing a member, disconnecting Google and deleting one person's login are not organization-closure requests. Closing one organization must not delete a shared user identity or another organization's records. P3/D6 governs refund of unused purchased AI balance; closure never converts included allowance into cash.

**Closure mechanics:** stop admitting new writes, reconcile in-flight canonical effects and revoke organization-scoped runtime/connector credentials. Preserve only the restricted access needed for authorized export and canceling closure; no new submissions or background AI actions. Canceling closure does not silently republish pages or restore revoked grants. Google files remain in their external owner's account; remove Coach House bindings/grants, not entire external files. A separately authorized source deletion must finish or report blocked before disconnecting its credential. At the deadline, export delays do not silently extend retention; show the deadline in advance and report failed cleanup explicitly.

**Lifecycle schedule — proposed engineering defaults, subject to measured qualification before activation:**

| Data class | Retention / deletion rule | Required boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Canonical responses, including staff-corrected answers | Until authorized deletion or the explicit configured retention rule; closure follows the approved 30-day window | No age-based default purge; deleting a placement or archiving a plan does not delete its source |
| Individually deleted Coach House response | Deny access at accepted deletion; target removal from live controlled stores within 24 hours; no new user-facing trash feature in this release | Confirm irreversible intent; include derived excerpts and controlled exports. Pending/failed purge is not completed erasure |
| Google response deletion | Delete only the stable identified response through a qualified authorized adapter | Recheck identity after row movement; no row-number-only delete, whole-file deletion or promise to erase provider history. Revoked access reports blocked |
| Raw response caches / telemetry | No durable answer cache; request-local processing only; exclude answers from logs and traces | Authorized browser view memory is cleared on scope exit/revocation where controlled. Already downloaded copies cannot be recalled |
| Temporary Coach House-generated exports | Expire download authorization and delete temporary artifact within 24 hours | Recheck access at generation and download; background generation cannot expand export rights. User-downloaded copies have separate ownership |
| Minimal intake delivery receipts | Terminal records: 30 days after resolution; unresolved records: at most 90 days from admission, followed by expiry without claiming a successful submission | No answer bodies or unnecessary respondent identity. Admission credentials bind a fixed expiry: a purged receipt never makes an expired operation eligible for a new write. Unknown outcome is not proven absence; never resubmit automatically |
| Controlled backups and object history | Use the verified configured recovery horizon, disclosed separately from live deletion | Inventory database, object storage, PITR, manual exports and log drains. Do not assume database backup includes uploaded files or promise a per-row purge from immutable backups |
| Deletion suppression records | Minimal opaque identifiers until every backup capable of restoring the deleted data has expired or been safely retired | Restore in isolation; replay deletions/revocations before reopening access, subscriptions or AI retrieval. Protect suppression records independently of the database restore point |

The receipt schedule applies to public intake recovery only. It does not shorten canonical run/application history, payment records or security evidence by analogy. Those existing owners must have separately documented purposes and retention; answer content may not be retained as billing evidence. Any exceptional retention obligation needs a named basis, restricted scope and end/review condition; do not invent a universal legal-hold system for MVP.

**Qualification, not a new product choice:** before activation, S07/S08 records actual configured backup/history/log horizons, expiry enforcement, deletion worker ownership and retry/alert behavior, and verifies the proposed time targets. If a target cannot be met, revise the published policy before launch; do not silently advertise it. No production settings were inspected or changed in this pass. Supabase documents plan/configuration-dependent database recovery windows and explicitly excludes Storage API object contents from database backups; source documentation is not evidence of our account settings. [Supabase backup documentation](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/backups)

**Required proof:** deleting a response removes its derived access; closing one organization leaves another untouched; an owner without dataset access cannot export answers; subscription cancellation does not delete data; an expired receipt cannot admit a duplicate write; uncertain Google outcomes never become successful by expiry; a restored backup cannot resurrect deleted records or revoked public grants; a disconnected Google account does not cause unrelated row/file deletion. Exercise worker failure and retries and independently inspect each controlled store. A documentation check alone passes none of these runtime gates.

### P5. Immediate submission and visible responses

**[ANSWERED D4 — user decision, October 29]** Submit directly to the selected canonical destination. Do not build a durable answer buffer, delayed delivery queue or 24-hour retry service. The buffer was proposed for provider-outage recovery; the user chose immediate submission instead. Coach House storage and Google Sheets remain supported destination choices. A response becomes available to authorized reviewers when its canonical write is confirmed, not after a batch or scheduled delivery.

**Submit contract:** validate the immutable published form version, audience, destination, request limits and answers; establish a stable submission identity and minimal recovery record; perform the destination write during the bounded submission request. Return success only after canonical persistence is confirmed. For Google, verify the destination row/reference through the qualified adapter; for Coach House, confirm the database commit. An idempotency record contains no retained Google response body and does not turn into a delivery queue.

| State / event | Behavior | User-visible truth |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Editing | Keep answers in the current form session; do not expose partial typing as submitted responses | Editable form |
| Submitting | Disable duplicate dispatch, preserve current answers and submission identity; perform direct validated write | Submitting |
| Confirmed write | Return canonical receipt/reference; invalidate the authorized response view and display the new response | Submitted; reviewer sees confirmed data |
| Proven failure before write | Keep answers in the current form; allow deliberate retry after correction or restored access | Not submitted; retry available |
| Timeout / lost connection after dispatch | Keep answers and original identity; query outcome before allowing another write | Checking submission; do not claim failure or success |
| Confirmed prior write on recovery | Return the existing receipt without issuing another write | Submitted once |
| Outcome remains unknown | Retain identity-only reconciliation where permitted; offer status/contact and block blind duplicate submission | Submission unconfirmed |
| Destination unavailable / access revoked / schema mismatch | Fail safely; do not switch storage or accept answers for later background delivery | Not submitted if absence is proven; otherwise unconfirmed |

**No retained answer queue:** Google-bound answers exist only in the respondent's active form state and necessary in-flight processing, then at Google after delivery. Exclude raw answers from server logs, tracing, durable job payloads, dead-letter queues and platform backups. No automatic offline queue, local-storage answer archive or promised draft recovery after the browser closes. Normal browser/server memory during request handling is not a new delivery store. Coach House-selected responses remain canonical platform records under the approved retention policy.

**Visible as submissions arrive:** the private response view uses the same destination adapter and authorization as submission/readback. A confirmed local write triggers authorized view invalidation/subscription updates; Google writes trigger source re-read rather than displaying a second canonical copy. An already-open review view updates without requiring a full page reload, using supported subscriptions or bounded refresh while visible. On reconnect/focus, re-fetch and show stale/unavailable state if the source cannot be read. Respect active filters/pagination: update authorized counts and offer a new-response affordance without jumping the reviewer's selection or overwriting their cell-edit draft. Responses submitted through Coach House and later edits made directly at Google must remain distinguishable. Direct Google changes use the adapter's supported freshness mechanism, not an invented instant-push guarantee.

**Duplicate safety:** double-click, concurrent requests and a lost success response must resolve to one canonical submission. A stable ID alone does not prove remote deduplication: qualify the Google adapter's destination identity, concurrency and reconciliation strategy before enabling it. Do not retry a write whose absence is unproven. Receipt lookup requires an unguessable capability or authenticated scoped access; a submission UUID alone is insufficient. Do not collect an email address just to support recovery. A receipt never grants response editing or access to other submissions.

**Scope:** complete submitted responses appear promptly. This decision does not authorize keystroke capture, live viewing of unfinished applications, respondent editing after submission or autosaving incomplete responses. P4 records approved 30-day organization closure; controlled backup and receipt schedules still require technical qualification. No additional product questionnaire is needed for basic form operation.

### P6. Policy acceptance and remaining decisions

Specification fixtures must cover:

1. An ordinary workspace editor without form-collaborator or response access cannot read a private response table; authorized form creators/editors/managers can.
2. A form creator/editor/manager can view new responses and correct a name/email cell without another reviewer setup; an external form editor cannot enumerate neighboring forms or records.
3. Linking a Sheet neither lends the connector's full identity to teammates nor creates Google grants. Protected cells and unqualified concurrent writes stay unavailable.
4. Dropping a local table offers an explicit imported copy and audience; dropping an existing document preserves its original source permissions.
5. Revocation between preview and apply denies the write and clears authorized cached views. Assignment alone changes no grant.
6. Immediate write confirmation, proven failure, revoked provider access and unknown remote outcomes produce distinct receipts. Lost responses/double-clicks do not duplicate submissions; answers remain in the active form for safe retry. No durable answer queue exists. Already-open authorized review views update from confirmed canonical submissions without a full page reload; filters and edit drafts remain intact.
7. Two simultaneous AI requests compete against one available balance correctly; duplicate payment events/objects grant once; unknown settlement cannot double charge.
8. No AI route, access grant or purchase policy is activated merely by editing this planning document. A retry of the original submission cannot overwrite a later staff correction.

**Policy decisions updated.** Latest user clarification simplifies forms: creators/managers/editors see and correct responses, no respondent uploads/edits, familiar question controls, optional Google Forms link-out, and 30-day explicit organization closure. This supersedes separate reviewer setup and annotation-only correction. Immediate submission and managed OpenAI/owner purchases/no auto-recharge remain approved. Commercial quantities and technical source/retention qualification remain explicit; P3 now records approved allowance/reset/carryover/refund behavior. S01–S11 reconciliation is recorded in section 9; section 15 records the completed consistency/coverage review and remaining commercial/qualification gates. Complete-plan approval remains required before application implementation.

##### Preservation and security dependencies — November11 amendment

**Data preservation is non-negotiable.** Infrastructure changes must preserve every user's uploaded files and bytes, file versions, documents, notes, form responses, canvas records, plans, relationships, permissions and connected-provider references. Use backward-compatible migrations and preserve canonical identities, revisions and references, including published/guest copies and their independent access/withdrawal. Never silently delete, overwrite, orphan or disconnect user data; never delete unknown Storage objects. Authorized product edits/deletions retain their existing explicit scope; migration is not deletion authorization.

**Migration acceptance:** reconcile affected records, bytes, identities, relationships, grants and provider references before and after the change; counts alone do not prove preservation. Verify existing clients/readers/writers remain compatible and perform independent readback. Before a risky migration/cutover, verify recovery for its exact affected data using existing backups/snapshots or a lossless rollback/forward-repair path, including stored bytes and access state; a written rollback plan or metadata-only backup is insufficient. Missing recovery proof or unexplained differences block that change, not unrelated development. Record evidence in the existing checkpoint; do not build a second recovery system.

**Required versus deferred:** finish essential legacy folder-binding/Storage cutover, tenant isolation, permissions, revocation, secure writes, compatibility, existing-data preservation and safe migration. Reuse qualified implementation; reopen it only for a concrete regression or changed dependency. Previously excluded independent historical-restore/deletion-revocation infrastructure, self-service organization closure and speculative security expansion remain deferred. Verified recovery for the migration being performed is required; it does not reopen the deferred historical-restore program or authorize privacy/closure activation.

Local internal admission proof is not activation proof; migration80000 remains unapplied. |

Before disclosure or apply, use the canonical current source/permission checks; derived indexes, snippets, caches and guidance cannot grant access or disclose revoked source content. Unknown lineage is not permission. |

Each enabled real path still needs its own authorization, source freshness/revocation, provider, persistence and output evidence. ##### Approved refinements: prototype, memory, funding and folder access — November5

**Decision source:** Caleb accepted the preceding recommendations except where corrected here: metered clarification/off-topic use is not free; account settings must manage memory; funding results should become useful application plans; and document folders/workspace context need real access boundaries. These refinements are approved product direction, not a claim of implementation. Preserve the rest of the [production sequence](#production-scope-and-execution-order--november5). No provider calls, external messages, new payment activation or production writes are authorized by accepting the design.

**Meter usage, not subjective usefulness — P3/S05.** A successfully completed metered answer, clarification or off-topic exchange consumes the selected organization's credits under its disclosed versioned tariff. Do not classify replies as free because the assistant considers them unhelpful, unrelated to the workspace or only a question. Remove the assistant's earlier free-clarification proposal. Deterministic UI actions, ordinary reads/edits, reopening history and retrieving an already paid result do not initiate a new inference charge. Internal decision/generation/tool costs belong to the operation quote and existing exposure ledger, not additional surprise charges. Platform-funded background indexing with finite limits and owner-selected default member caps are accepted; a new member has no AI allowance until an explicit default/override exists, and existing members are not silently changed. The prior failed/canceled-run zero-customer-charge policy remains distinct and unchanged; all incurred provider cost still counts against service limits. Never use failure/cancellation to create unbounded free provider work. Actual tariff quantities remain measured commercial values, not inferred approval of invented prices.

**Deterministic first; very concise user replies — S04/S05/S10/E3.** Use registered code paths for known commands, permission filtering, validation, source reads, calculations, deadlines, dependency transitions, rendering and layout. Use models for interpretation, evidence synthesis, writing and genuinely uncertain judgments. Do not add a model call where a deterministic handler can finish the action. Default assistant output to the fewest words that convey the answer, necessary question or result; no preamble, repeated plan narration, unsolicited reasoning essay or routine internal accounting/status copy. Ask only for missing information that changes the result or blocks a required step, and retrieve permitted existing information first. Put generated application/document content in its editable artifact, rather than repeating it in chat. Keep essential uncertainty, action confirmation and expandable source evidence available; brevity must not omit a material constraint or corrupt an application answer. These are shared behavior/evaluation rules, not a UI redesign or an arbitrary word cap on requested artifacts.

**Prototype reuse and executable plan grammar — S01/S02/S05/S10.** Reference root: `/Users/calebhamernick/Development/Reverse-engineer/offloop-flow`. Inspection found the existing Board Portal study at localhost:3028, source `app/src/main.jsx` (`FlowNode`, `NodeEditor`, `FlowCanvas`) and `app/src/model.mjs` (`step`, `transition`, `layout`); contracts are in `docs/system.md` and `docs/style-system.md`. Compact nodes expand inline, human assignees sit beneath, parallel branches join, evidence belongs inside the expanded node, and review/repair actions are explicit. Layout reserves expanded bounds. This is a local simulation, not a production writer or permission system. Its fixture assignees, simulated work, browser storage, runtime architecture suggestions and display-only expert price must not be transplanted. Current inspection used source and saved `evidence/canvas-only.png`; the server returned200, but the browser-control host was unavailable, so no fresh interactive verification is claimed.

Extend the existing Particle/capability registry into the following bounded composition contract; do not create a second graph/runtime or permit AI-authored JSX/CSS:

| Plan element | Permitted data / canonical authority | Presentation and actual operation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Objective/plan | Existing objective/plan identity, title, outcome, memberships and revisions | Existing board projection; propose/edit through the same plan writer. |
| Work step | Short title, editable brief/checklist, eligible human assignee, relevant dates, source/artifact references | Compact existing node; inline expansion/editor with a real save path. No agent avatar pretending to be a teammate. |
| Decision / missing information | Precise question, supported choices or typed response, evidence, authorized decider and outcome-linked dependencies | Existing decision/form controls; answers update the owning record and recompute only affected readiness/branches. Unknown requirements remain explicit. |
| Working artifact | Existing registered note/document/form/table/opportunity type, source ID, revision, allowed editable fields and provenance | Render the real artifact/editor. A filename or prose promise is not a created document/form. |
| Dependency / branch / join | Stable endpoint IDs, supported relation/outcome and required-versus-optional participation | Deterministic graph validation/layout. Never copy the prototype's generic completed-node count over the approved progress contract. No arbitrary autonomous loops. |
| Evidence and proposed effect | Source location/revision, extraction coverage, proposed changes, approval state and execution receipt when applicable | Details on demand; a referenced source grants no new access and a proposal is never labeled completed execution. |

Each registration must bind input/output schemas, allowed child/content slots and bounds, canonical reader/editor/writer, action/permission and revision checks, capability availability and result rendering. AI chooses from permitted registrations and proposes typed data/operations; code validates and places it. Make title/brief/assignment/content editable through existing controls before calling a generated element usable. Preserve stable identity through revision and canonical Add/whole-plan drag. Use measured, deterministic layout with existing locked/manual positions, clearances and reduced-motion behavior; the model does not decide CSS, pixel coordinates or new controls. Clicking a node need not open fullscreen or a new sidebar. Adding results to the workspace uses existing Add; placing selected content on a shared/public page remains the separate existing explicit publication flow, with audience/source/asset review. Do not interpret “add to page” as permission to publish private material. No mandatory transfer of the prototype's appearance to all current particles.

**Memory in account settings — K8/S05.** The user does not have to type a special command to manage saved guidance. Add Memory to the existing account settings menu; follow the supplied screenshots' compact Enable memory control, readable Memory summary with updated time, close action and overflow containing About memory and Delete and turn off memory. Provide inspect/add/edit/delete through that same settings surface using existing primitives; an explicit conversational save request is an additional route to the same writer, not the only route. A summary is a projection of saved entries, not a separately invented factual biography. Do not import facts or prices from the screenshot into organization records.

Keep private, organization-scoped preferences separate from explicitly authorized shared organization guidance. Show the scope before saving; shared changes require the existing management authority. A personal toggle cannot disable or erase the entire team's guidance. Turning memory off stops using/saving it for that scope; Delete and turn off also removes that scope's retained guidance and invalidates derived context/index entries. It does not delete chats, accepted plans/documents or required accounting records. Settings changes and saved-guidance correction/deletion must affect subsequent retrieval. No automatic extraction of personal/team memories is implied; it remains deferred unless separately requested. Reuse the approved settings placement and compact dialog style; no independent memory dashboard or control on every chat message.

**Funding discovery → application decision tree — S04/S05/S10.** Finding a potential opportunity is the beginning. Retrieve the actual application instructions, eligibility, award terms, deadline/timezone, required documents/answers, word/format limits, match/reporting obligations and submission steps where accessible. Preserve source URLs/versions/checked time and distinguish known requirements, inferred planning suggestions and unanswered facts. When instructions are unavailable or behind an inaccessible portal, say which parts are missing; never fabricate the application outline.

Build an editable plan using the registered grammar: eligibility/go-no-go decision → necessary evidence/questions → narrative/budget/attachment drafts in parallel where independent → required review → user-owned submission step. Reuse permitted organization documents and facts first. Questions belong to the affected step and ask only for gaps; never invent accomplishments, financials, commitments or answers to meet eligibility. Accepted answers feed the same draft/source owner with revisions. Preserve unrelated work and allow iterative chat or direct edits before adding to the board; continue the same artifacts after Add. Drafting never sends outreach, submits an application, signs certifications or guarantees funding.

Support opportunity-cost comparison with explicit inputs: eligibility fit, verified deadline, award range/restrictions, estimated staff effort, required cash match and ongoing obligations. Deterministic calculations compare cost/effort when inputs are known; estimates and user assumptions are labeled. Do not invent win probabilities or expected returns. Explain priority in a short reason, with evidence/details on demand. The accepted initial research mode is on-demand, saved and refreshable; “last7days” uses source-reported publication/material update, with discovery time separate. Evaluate real requirement coverage, faithful drafts, missing-information questions, preservation and useful prioritization, not just the number of found grants. Broader funding-provider expansion still requires an explicit supported-source contract.

**Folders, workspace audiences and AI context — P2/S04/S09/S11; required MVP scope.** Reuse existing organization/project file browsing and folder interactions. Inspected owners: `member-workspace/lib/project-asset-folders.ts`, `server/project-asset-folder-actions.ts`, `components/projects/project-asset-folders.tsx`, composed by `member-workspace-project-detail-tabs.tsx`. Existing `assetFolders` stores folder ID/name and file placements in project options, with create/rename/remove/move and project-level authorization/revision guards; it has no folder audience/ACL fields. Existing organization document access and Particle source checks are reusable enforcement points, not proof of private folder isolation. Named canvases also appear in organization board state; a canvas label or hidden UI is not an access boundary. Qualify the actual server/DB workspace-scope model before adding department isolation.

Required behavior:

- Users can create folders and choose their permitted audience: private, explicitly invited people, or selected workspace audiences using existing View/Edit/Manage capabilities. Workspace audiences such as Finance, Board, Communications, Home and Programs are configurable scopes, not hardcoded universal roles. Board/Finance may be granted several folders; Communications may be granted Home/Programs while denied Finance/Board. Neither assignment nor a workspace name grants access. Invitations grant only the reviewed resource scope after identity verification; do not grant organization administration or AI spending implicitly.
- Enforce actor/organization membership, workspace audience, owning-folder/document permission and external source authority together. A shared folder cannot lend its owner's Drive access. Preserve existing access during migration; do not turn all files private/public based on a guessed default or bulk copy them into a new store.
- One canonical document retains its identity. Folder placement/aliases and board references do not create independent grants or duplicate content. Private/invite-only must protect the document's actual read/download/edit/search routes, not merely hide a folder. Moving a file across different audiences must check and disclose the access change before committing it; linking into a broader folder cannot silently widen access. If nesting is introduced, inherit parent access by default and allow narrowing; exceptions require an explicit reviewed grant, not accidental union of every linked folder.
- Workspace context is an explicit set of eligible folders/sources, intersected with the requesting user's permissions. Being personally authorized for Finance does not automatically inject Finance into a Communications chat. Explicitly selected additional context still needs source access and an appropriate result audience; a broad shared-board artifact cannot silently disclose a private source through generated text. Review/scope the result or remove restricted content before broader sharing.
- Apply the same policy to folder/document names, counts, +/@ discovery, body extraction, keyword/vector results, caches, saved guidance, citations, restored source-derived messages, generated previews, downloads and edits. Filter before model disclosure and recheck current authority before writes. Revocation invalidates affected derived data and prevents new access; moving a document or adding a Particle cannot bypass it.
- Reuse folder rows, search, existing access controls and invitation patterns. No new dashboard. Verify owner/member/invitee/outsider cases, Board-versus-Communications context, multi-folder references, revoked access, concurrent moves/grants, lost replies and existing-record migration against actual server/DB and file paths.

**Sequence adjustment:** define the workspace/folder source-access contract alongside row1's minimal catalog, and implement/qualify it in row2 before broad connected-folder retrieval or indexing. Keep row1 durable-chat progress independent where it uses already-authorized sources. Row3 owns the prototype-derived typed plan/artifact lifecycle; row7 now includes application plans/drafts/questions and opportunity-cost comparison. Memory settings ship with row2 guidance. Open in Sheets for Google-response corrections is accepted; native corrections remain in-app, and safe form-to-Sheets delivery remains required. The previous free-clarification and “saved guidance only by typing” interpretations must not reappear. Update the existing owners/tests rather than start another roadmap.

**What “continue” means:**

1. Resume the current unfinished ready group using this checkpoint and valid evidence. Do not restart discovery/planning, reopen settled decisions or ask permission for already authorized local work. Continue into the next ready group when its prerequisites permit; a commit or completed agent task is not a reason to stop by itself.
2. Assign independent implementation/acceptance outcomes to parallel agents, each with its own dedicated goal and non-overlapping file ownership. Keep one integration owner for shared schema/writers. Parallel review of one tiny change does not substitute for advancing an independent ready outcome.
3. Freeze each group's existing requirement/case list at entry. Add a substep only for a demonstrated dependency or failing contract; record the requirement, evidence and effect on completion. Unrelated improvements and further SDK/UI migrations stay outside this work. Never remove required scope merely to close a group.
4. Batch related implementation, focused verification, required Graphify maintenance and checkpoint/mirror updates at usable boundaries. Preserve valid proof until affected code/configuration/dependencies/environment invalidate it. Do not rerun passing broad suites or rebuild fixtures for reassurance.
5. For a true external blocker, name the exact missing account, data, setting, spend cap, commercial decision or action authorization; prepare the concrete reviewable packet first. Continue independent ready work. Elapsed time is not approval. If no authorized work remains, report **local work complete; external gates blocked**, not whole-plan complete.
6. At a usable boundary update this section's resume state, the affected packet evidence and concise runlog/index/original-packet pointers; synchronize Downloads/Desktop mirrors and save scoped work locally. Report **outcome closed, remaining blocker, next ready group**. Do not use file/test counts or estimated percentages as product progress. Retire this section's pending entry inventories once populated; do not repeat them on each “continue.”

### Execution policy — fast delivery within fixed contracts

**Apply the deeper-thinking framework once, then by exception.** A senior engineer would identify the smallest complete interaction, canonical owners and actual failure boundaries before adding infrastructure. Start from current schemas, writers, saved records, permissions, traces and existing test evidence—not feature descriptions alone. Use targeted source/graph inspection, typed runtime contracts, bounded integration slices and risk-based verification. Independent proof is canonical readback, denied-access checks, preserved unrelated state, measured behavior and required CI; neither the model's confidence nor a plausible preview is proof. Reassess only when changed evidence, dependencies or failures materially affect a decision.

**Each authorized packet begins with four short lines, derived from this spec:**
- **Outcome:** observable usable behavior within authorized scope.
- **Changes:** existing owners and necessary edits; no speculative framework.
- **Constraints:** applicable contracts, dependencies and approval boundaries.
- **Verification:** smallest sufficient checks and explicit completion condition.

Then execute. Make routine implementation choices autonomously. Resolve technical details when their packet needs them; do not reopen settled product decisions or demand implementation detail for future capabilities first. Build the complete supported path before generalizing variations: create, review where required, apply, edit, reload and recover. This delivery order does not reduce required MVP scope. Start dependency work with the smallest actual integration and expand only for concrete uncertainty.

Preserve all approved functionality while reducing process: no speculative infrastructure, competing registries/stores/execution engines/plans, or silent deferral/removal/simplification. Use the smallest complete end-to-end implementation and proportional checks of changed behavior, data preservation and critical invariants; do not repeat investigations or qualification without changed evidence.

Use parallel agents only for independent work with clear ownership, stable interfaces and one integration owner; no duplicate reconnaissance or mandatory agent count per phase. Reuse source context and verification until invalidated. Batch Graphify and checkpoint updates according to repository rules. Authorized routine reversible edits need no extra review ceremony; existing owner approval of AI proposals, publication and consequential-action authority remain intact. Do not claim undo/history exists where it has not been implemented.

Stop verification when the packet outcome and applicable gates pass. Continue automatically only into the next explicitly authorized packet; stop at the end of authorized scope. Reopen planning only for a concrete contradiction, blocked dependency, failed contract or missing decision that changes scope or risk. A routine implementation detail is not a permission question. Report outcome, evidence and material unresolved gates briefly. October 30 authorization starts S01 implementation and completion tracking; this policy does not authorize paid evaluation, deployment or external effects. Continue later packets only within explicit authorization.

**Reusable execution prompt:**
> Implement [authorized packet] in the existing Coach House stack. Deliver [its usable outcome] using its registered capabilities and canonical writers. Follow the specified selection, editing, navigation, motion and recovery behavior; keep the interface minimal, focused and consistent with existing tokens and surfaces. Output working UI, state and persistence, plus one concise checkpoint. Begin with Outcome / Changes / Constraints / Verification, then execute. Reuse valid context and evidence. Run the smallest sufficient affected checks; expand only for relevant shared contracts, permissions, money, external effects, failures or required release gates. Stop when completion criteria pass. Continue only through authorized packets. Ask only for a material unresolved decision; preserve required approvals. Do not add scope, arbitrary effects, new frameworks or repeated broad planning.

**Shared packet contract:** A1–A5 owns authority; B1–B5 owns selected dependencies; U1–U12 and V01–V14 own presentation; H/K owns planning/context/tools; L1–L7 owns admission, operation identities, events and recovery; P1–P6 owns policy; O1–O8 owns source output bindings; E1–E8 owns proof. Packet text binds these contracts, not a competing copy of their rules. Type checks validate shape; runtime schemas, authorization, revisions, semantic validation and canonical readback remain independent gates.

**Source versus new work:** source paths below are inspected anchors, not a claim that every listed integration exists. Recheck the affected owner at implementation entry. Preserve current saved records and compatible schemas; any necessary new fields have version/migration/rollback fixtures. Existing functionality closes a requirement with evidence. An empty interface, fixture-only preview or schema-only package does not close the usable outcome.

**Approved scope versus readiness:** manual editing, supported sharing, immediate form intake, private response review, saved editable source views and AI credit purchases are required where named. A failed adapter may remain disabled during development, but silently omitting required functionality is not an MVP release. Public response-backed views depend on separate explicit publication support; private response review is the required default.

###### Document embedding provider configuration proposal — November11

**Completed outcome: reviewable configuration, not activation.** The preceding Next paragraph is fulfilled by this proposal. Provider documentation qualifies the public contract below; it does not prove this account's settings, availability, billed usage, retrieval quality or live access. **Caleb approved this configuration for the following offline transport slice; activation remains separately unauthorized.** Original workstream08 stages1/3 and primary-list row2 retain ownership; no new plan, registry or accounting authority is introduced.

| Decision | Proposed configuration |
| --- | --- |
| Provider/model | OpenAI API, exact `text-embedding-3-small`,1536 dimensions, synchronous `POST https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings`, `encoding_format: float`. This fits the existing2000-dimension limit at its native size. No alternate-provider fallback or Batch API. [Model](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/text-embedding-3-small), [dimensions](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/embeddings#how-to-get-embeddings). |
| Price | Standard input **$0.02 per million tokens**; `microdollarsPerMillion: 20000`. This is the documented list rate, not an account-specific discount or a new customer tariff. [Published price](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/text-embedding-3-small). |
| Destination/terms | Standard OpenAI endpoint; **no regional residency commitment**. Embeddings have no retained application state. Default abuse-monitoring logs may retain content for up to30days, with longer legal or harm-prevention exceptions. API data is not used for training unless the customer opts in. Before enabling, verify the intended project has no sharing/training opt-in and disclose its actual terms. Zero Data Retention eligibility is not evidence that this account has it. [Provider data controls](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data). |
| Eligible content | Initially at most **five exact native editor `document:<section-id>` records** in one reviewed nonproduction org/actor/canvas scope. Require a current canonical revision, readable nonempty text, qualified lineage and actor AND canvas authority on every run. The qualification allowlist starts empty; IDs and exact scope must be evidenced before activation. Membership in the allowlist never grants access. |
| Source boundary | Only normalized text chunks and the retrieval query go to this embedding endpoint. The existing answer-model context remains separate. Uploaded `file:*`, Drive, Sheets, unknown document/particle origins, restricted sources awaiting the failed cache/cutover gate and independent guest/published copies are excluded from this first provider qualification. Those capabilities remain MVP work, not silently removed scope. |
| Bounds | `maxInputBytes: 180000` per request; `maxInputTokens: 200000` cumulative per run; `maxCalls: 8` including query embeddings. Retain the existing9600 UTF-16 units/source,480-unit chunks/400-unit stride and160-unit query. Transport must additionally reject inputs exceeding1440 UTF-8 bytes each. Five sources produce at most120 chunks; even the conservative120×1440=172800-byte bound fits. |

Add this to the existing answer-model reservation; the combined$0.25/125-credit ceilings remain enforced. Customer credits follow the existing approved `microdollarsPerCredit` conversion and combined rounding; no subscription, allowance, margin or free-processing rule changes. |

**Tokenizer qualification and its limits.** Current [OpenAI guidance](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/embeddings#how-can-i-tell-how-many-tokens-a-string-has-before-i-embed-it) specifies `cl100k_base`; the [official tokenizer example](https://developers.openai.com/cookbook/examples/how_to_count_tokens_with_tiktoken) exposes each token's bytes. Local inspection of the already-installed tiktoken0.4.0 verifies all100256 ordinary vocabulary entries are nonempty/reversible and all256 single bytes exist;266 synthetic ordinary-encoding cases round-trip and stay below their UTF-8 byte counts. This supports the structural inference that ordinary byte-pair encoding cannot produce more tokens than input bytes; it is not an API usage measurement or a claim that the old package supplies a current model mapping. Current documentation supplies that mapping. No package was installed/upgraded. Tokenizer receipt: `.tmp/embedding-provider-proposal-20261111/tokenizer.json`, exact vocabulary digest and elapsed9.589s.

The [endpoint contract](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/embeddings/methods/create) permits8192tokens/input,2048 input strings and300000tokens/request. Proposed1440-byte individual/180000-byte request bounds stay below these limits under the qualified ordinary tokenizer. Treat special-looking source text as ordinary content; reject malformed Unicode before dispatch instead of silently transforming canonical text. Preserve normalized-reader offsets. The transport's later offline checks must cover these wire boundaries and actual usage reconciliation; changed tokenizer/model behavior invalidates this qualification. No character-to-token average is used.

**User-confirmed direction:** the small native-document embedding pilot is a qualification boundary, not a product-capacity ceiling. Coach House must analyze the organization’s working information: mission/vision/values, formation and registration records, budgets/financials, people, meetings and committee work, governance, strategic/program/impact documents, compliance/legal records and historical archives. **Chosen first evaluation:** an evidence-backed readiness brief for the November 12, 2026 board meeting: what decisions are needed, how proposals fit mission/strategy, what the current budget and actuals establish, applicable governance/registration constraints, unresolved earlier decisions/actions and responsible people/committees. Identify missing, contradictory, outdated or inaccessible evidence. Distinguish an agenda proposal from approved minutes, a recorded resolution, a vote or a completed action. A draft analysis neither casts votes nor changes records, assignments or approvals. Opportunity-fit analysis is a subsequent use of the same organization evidence with verified opportunity terms/deadlines; public research remains separately qualified.

**Required processing behavior:**
- **Documents and archives:** discover all authorized sources within the selected scope, preserve heading/paragraph/table/page or normalized-text locations where the parser actually supports them, and retrieve/read additional passages as needed. Large-document processing must reach relevant content beyond today’s prefix limits. Whole-document review requires complete coverage or an explicit incomplete result; a handful of excerpts cannot stand in for full review. Support bounded pages/batches and resumable processing where necessary, with cancellation, progress, missing/failed-source accounting and measured resource/cost limits. Unsupported formats/OCR remain visible gaps, not empty documents or silently completed work.
- **Tables and financial data:** retain typed columns, row identities, dates/periods, units/currencies, nulls and source formula results. Filter, group, total and compare using deterministic trusted handlers over a complete declared selection; do not ask a model to infer totals from semantically selected rows. Cite the exact table/tab/range, filters and source revision; never present a sample or partial page as an all-row total. Qualify pagination/snapshot consistency and explicit partial failures before increasing scale. General in-app Sheets editing remains deferred; reading/analyzing is separate.
- **Current and historical evidence:** use current source readers and record checked time, effective/reporting period and version/status. Preserve history and explain superseded/conflicting records rather than treating the newest upload as automatically authoritative. Revalidate permissions and changed inputs before answers/reopen/apply. Different external systems do not provide an invented atomic snapshot.

These counts are requirements context, not a new audit of imported content. Original and optimized hierarchies are alternative views over the same canonical lessons/questions/answers/outputs. Do not duplicate questions or invent the missing exact question text/input types.

Indexes remain derived and permissions remain current. Evaluate any sharing/reuse across actors or workspaces before adoption; no permission bypass or competing factual store. Large libraries must not require resending the whole library for each question.

**Evaluation and acceptance:** use controlled fixtures first, then a separately approved representative source set. Cover mission/program/governance evidence, exact budget-versus-actual calculations, older/current/conflicting versions, late-document evidence, multi-passage answers, inaccessible committee material, missing inputs and retained-result invalidation. Compare keyword-only and hybrid retrieval against known expected evidence/answers, including correct abstention. **Implementation status: In progress — workspace-only disclosure, current-context/source revalidation and versioned evidence coverage with contact-search minimization and saved-result dependency checks implemented locally. Return/reconnect invalidation, visible saved-source coverage, typed saved-result recovery and admission/uncertain-reservation recovery are implemented locally. Fine-grained disclosure, remaining context/tool failure contracts, live authorization qualification and approved public-research boundary remain open.**

- [x] **Private-context research cannot offer public web search.** `research-provider.ts` exposes only `search_workspace` and `read_workspace`, regardless of legacy search-budget configuration. Final round exposes no tools. Calls to unoffered tools stop without dispatch. Generated URL annotations are not admitted as source evidence. Workspace citations and proposal/review/reload remain on their existing path.
- [x] **Capability and quote agree.** `research-v4-workspace` invalidates stale quotes; reservations exclude unavailable search and no longer require its pricing configuration. UI states “Uses workspace sources. Web search is unavailable.” Read-tool descriptions distinguish internal retrieval from disclosure to the configured model. No new processing/provider approval is inferred.
- [x] **Unexpected provider activity remains recoverable.** Unexpected built-in web-search output fails to the existing correlated-run reconciliation path; it cannot produce an accepted proposal or a zero-cost success. This contains application tool exposure; it does not claim control over a provider that violates its request contract.
- [x] **Recheck context and source snapshots locally.** Tool operations reload the actor-authorized target; reject actor/canvas changes and stale target revisions. Before each model dispatch and final result, compare selected-plan members and disclosed records against current exact-ID readers. Missing, revoked, changed or unavailable evidence stops the run without another provider dispatch or successful proposal; already transmitted data cannot be recalled. No permission-blind search/result cache remains. Repeated searches reload current records; profile reads coalesce only inside a fresh check. File extraction alone is cached per run, behind fresh entitlement and exact file metadata checks. Freshness reads use groups of at most four and honor run cancellation/deadline checks between bounded operations. Final application uses exact source IDs too; the existing canonical writer and ledger remain authoritative.
- [x] **Versioned evidence and bounded contact search:** tool responses and persisted citations carry server-produced v1 coverage (`metadata_only`, `excerpt`, `complete`, `unavailable`), extraction scope, checked/read timestamps and disclosed UTF-16 character counts. Complete means the approved record projection or declared extraction scope, never the entire underlying entity. Selected-plan metadata never claims a body read. Citation binding and later search do not upgrade or erase stronger read evidence. Historical citations without coverage remain unknown, not backfilled. Search uses contact names/roles only; contact routes, notes and provenance require a selected authorized read. Tool responses explicitly project allowed fields, excluding reader internals. Duplicate read IDs share one read/budget allocation; upstream 20,000-character clipping is reported. `research-v5-evidence` invalidates older quotes after the tool/prompt contract change.
- [x] **Recheck saved citations before reopening:** saved successful results validate run/target provenance and re-read each cited workspace source through the current actor-authorized exact-ID reader. A missing, changed, unsupported or unavailable source withholds the whole result, including derived prose, rather than merely removing its citation. Application shares the same check; duplicate-request recovery cannot bypass it. Source reads run in groups of at most four. Fixed errors exclude private reader details; historical evidence is not upgraded. This proves cited-source checks only, not complete dependency tracking.
- [x] **Persist and recheck research dependencies:** successful new results retain a server-authored v1 manifest separate from visible citations. It fingerprints the exact initial organization-owned prompt projection, all observed workspace tool records (including uncited search/read inputs), selected-plan members and extracted file details. Reopening, duplicate-request recovery and new application reauthorize those dependencies through current readers; changes to the bounded content projection are detected even when revisions are null or unchanged. File reads repeat authorized extraction and compare the disclosed detail projection. Hashes/IDs are stored, not an extra copy of private input text. At most 256 dependencies are admitted, with source checks in groups of four; overflow cannot become a successful billed proposal. The model cannot author this manifest. Canonical plan validation excludes server metadata from model-output validation.
- [x] **Historical-result policy:** results without a complete dependency manifest remain stored but are withheld on reopen/new application with a concise request to research again. Do not fabricate missing provenance or silently upgrade old runs. Existing already-applied proposal history keeps its idempotent no-op behavior; this returns no saved research prose and performs no new write. Changed initial context conservatively invalidates a result, rather than labeling it current.
- [x] **Invalidate open research on return/reconnect:** returning focus, visible-tab activation and reconnection recheck the saved run through the existing server-authorized dependency reader. Hide derived content and block proposing while checks run or fail; coalesce overlapping events. Retry restores only a valid result. Known objective/plan staleness hides an already-open review immediately. Discard/target changes invalidate late responses; failed application requires a fresh status check. This is event-driven validation, not continuous polling or instantaneous cross-client revocation.
- [x] **Show saved source coverage:** cited sources use compact pills with explicit coverage and keyboard/touch-accessible details. Distinguish source details only, partial text, all available text within the declared scope, unavailable content and historical unknown coverage. Expanded details identify record/text/document-body/selected-plan limits and the original coverage timestamp; they do not imply a fresh read or verified facts. Keep an explicit source link and a no-citations state. Coverage comes from the existing server-authored envelope, never model prose. Current-view invalidation unmounts the review and its source details.
- [x] **Typed saved-result recovery:** a shared allowlist defines source-free failure codes and recovery actions. Failed readers withhold derived content and offer a fresh authorization/status check on the same run; they do not assert permanent revocation. Confirmed missing/changed dependencies, historical manifests, invalid saved output and scope mismatches require discarding the unusable result. Unknown context/ledger exceptions are redacted. UI uses the fixed code contract, retains the run and prompt, hides unusable actions and never regenerates automatically. Duplicate-request read failures retain the existing reservation/run ID, return a typed 409 and do not replay generation or settlement. This covers saved-result reads and shared application dependency validation; other admission/tool/provider failure contracts remain open.
- [x] **Admission and uncertain-reservation recovery:** quote/start actions return fixed source-free errors rather than raw context, configuration, schema or ledger exception text. Invalid requests fail before context access; oversized selected-plan context and changed pricing fail before reservation. Changed pricing requires closing/reopening to review a fresh quote; the stale quote cannot be resubmitted. A failed reservation transport is conservatively uncertain: keep the attempted run ID for status recovery, do not claim/generate/settle/reconcile an unconfirmed reservation, and never enable a second run automatically. Confirmed-run interruptions retain existing reconciliation even if reconciliation itself fails. Confirmed ledger rejection categories are implemented in the following checkpoint; actual lost-response qualification remains open.
- [ ] **Complete saved-result revocation:** qualify source-specific permission/revision behavior, authenticated revocation and external changes while the current tab remains active. Current checks use existing actor-authorized readers; they do not create fine-grained source permissions or instantaneous cross-client invalidation. Already disclosed, applied or downloaded content cannot be recalled by blocking a saved run.
- [x] **Confirmed admission denials:** eight exact, server-returned SQL rejection messages plus `P0001` map to credit shortage, usage limit, busy capacity or disabled AI. Source inspection verifies those branches follow the existing-run check under the admission lock; failed allocation rolls back in the existing transaction. Research shows fixed guidance, preserves the typed request and clears only the rejected attempt's recovery identity. No provider work, automatic retry, claim, settlement or reconciliation occurs for these confirmed denials. Access/revision/identity conflicts, unknown SQL errors, rejected transports and malformed successes remain uncertain; they never clear recovery identity merely because an error looks familiar. Existing non-research consumers retain the same Error messages. No SQL, ledger, permission or pricing changes.

- [x] **Deadline and cancellation stage fences:** the existing 90-second signal is checked before/after cancellation and source-validation reads, during/after provider streaming, and after tools return or fail. Late readers and caught tool aborts cannot start another stage or return a successful proposal. Observed cancellation between stages stops further dispatch and retains measured provider usage. Missing terminal usage/expired work throws into existing correlated recovery; it never fabricates zero spending or automatically regenerates. Eight-tool and final-round bounds remain enforced. This is local stage-boundary proof, not proof that non-abortable I/O stops immediately or live provider cancellation/accounting is qualified.

- [x] **Honest non-selected context coverage:** bounded objective overviews now disclose shown/total/omitted counts for plans, each shown plan's member IDs and pending proposal titles. Existing 4-plan/8-member/4-proposal limits remain; reviewed proposals do not inflate pending counts. Plan IDs/revisions disambiguate titles. These are summaries, never full reads; the model must inspect authorized records or request the relevant plan when omissions matter. Selected-plan context remains complete or rejected. Coverage participates in the existing byte budget and context fingerprint. `research-v6-context-coverage` invalidates older quotes. Existing saved runs whose old context fingerprints differ follow existing stale-result recovery; they are not silently rewritten or regenerated. This qualifies payload construction, not live model adherence or a claim that all organization work was read.

- [x] **Direct authorized reference reads:** `read_workspace` resolves known organization, person, core-document, uploaded-file, Particle, calendar and opportunity references through existing actor-scoped readers. Search is needed only when an ID is unknown. References cannot select arbitrary URLs, paths or new readers. Exact ID/kind matching, document entitlement, four-ID and detail-byte/character limits remain; duplicate IDs share one read. Successful reads retain evidence and dependency fingerprints for subsequent dispatch, reopening and application checks. Missing, denied, mismatched and failed reads return the same source-free error. Previously observed records still reject changes instead of silently rebasing. `research-v7-direct-read` invalidates older quotes; existing saved-result schemas/fingerprints are unchanged by this slice. Local fixtures do not establish live source permissions or processing approval.

- [ ] **Complete evidence and context contract:** source-specific/fine-grained disclosure rules, remaining tool/provider failure and recovery distinctions and remaining timeout/cancellation qualification. Preserve selected-plan context completely or reject oversize input; current format and result bounds remain. Local revalidation does not establish global instantaneous revocation or live provider/database qualification.

**Provider evidence and qualification verdict (documentation/source inspection, not a live test):**

| Concern | Documented primitive / exact gap | Gate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Append/retry | `values.append` appends after the detected table and can include returned values. Its documented request has no submission-id uniqueness or expected-revision parameter. A lost reply cannot justify appending again | Plain append plus read-before-write is unqualified for duplicate prevention. [Append contract](https://developers.google.com/workspace/sheets/api/reference/rest/v4/spreadsheets.values/append) |
| Atomicity versus concurrent corrections | `batchUpdate` applies its own valid requests atomically, but Google explicitly allows concurrent collaborators to alter the result. `UpdateCellsRequest` declares rows/fields/location, not an expected answer value/revision | An application revision check followed by an unconditional write cannot promise detection of direct-Sheet edits. No supported conflict strategy is qualified. [Batch contract](https://developers.google.com/workspace/sheets/api/reference/rest/v4/spreadsheets/batchUpdate), [cell writer](https://developers.google.com/workspace/sheets/api/reference/rest/v4/spreadsheets/request#UpdateCellsRequest) |
| Stable row identity | Developer metadata can attach identity to a row and locate it through a data filter. Metadata keys are not unique; metadata IDs are. Metadata is not secret storage or an access boundary | A provider-side unique marker in an atomic batch is a candidate for delivery deduplication, not proof of the entire intake/correction contract. Qualify marker collision/allocation, exact row binding, deletion, copied rows, delayed commits and retry expiry before enabling it. Metadata lookup does not itself compare answer revisions. [Metadata](https://developers.google.com/workspace/sheets/api/guides/metadata), [filtered writes](https://developers.google.com/workspace/sheets/api/reference/rest/v4/spreadsheets.values/batchUpdateByDataFilter) |
| Acting identity and protected cells | Drive exposes current-user capabilities; Sheets exposes protected-range restrictions separately | Existing file metadata reads do not establish interactive correction authority. Recheck the actual editor's access, formula/identity protection and destination restrictions; never substitute an owner's connection. Narrow manager-authorized public delivery is a separate delegation. [Drive capabilities](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/guides/manage-sharing), [protected ranges](https://developers.google.com/workspace/sheets/api/reference/rest/v4/spreadsheets/sheets#ProtectedRange) |

**Counterexamples the real adapter must defeat:** (1) write commits but reply is lost; retry races the original delayed operation; (2) app reads answer A, a person writes B in Sheets, app writes C using its earlier check; (3) row moves between lookup and positional update; (4) source permission or protection changes after preflight; (5) an original submission is retried after an authorized correction. App-only locks, a second read, a successful HTTP response and simulated tests alone do not defeat these schedules. These are analytical cases, not reported provider observations.

**Disposition:** keep native Sheets intake/correction unavailable, preserve it as unfinished scope, and continue the already-approved native form path. Do not silently introduce durable Google answer copies, Apps Script, service-account proxies, protected app-only Sheets or last-write-wins corrections. Those change the architecture or collaboration contract and require a scoped decision if adopted. Google Forms link-out remains a separate optional capability. A future live qualification uses an explicitly selected disposable Sheet and two authorized identities, bounded synthetic answers and independent provider readback; do not probe customer data. Passing live runs cannot establish a guarantee absent from the documented primitive.
