#### S12 (proposed follow-up). Connected organization payments, fundraising and recurring support

**Implementation status: [VERIFY] — the user reports that much of the Stripe account-connection path already exists. It has not been audited in this specification. This is a proposed, separately authorized follow-up; it does not amend the approved S01–S11 MVP, S05 credit billing, S11 release gate or the current deferral of end-user payment collection. Do not rebuild or migrate an existing integration on the strength of this section. Stripe developer-documentation qualification refreshed November 2, 2026; documentation alignment is not runtime qualification.**

- **Gate / dependencies:** inspect the existing Stripe connection, payment, webhook, finance and organization-access owners first; P2 source/permission rules, P3 billing separation, P4 closure rules, S06 reviewed public outputs and S07 asset rules where used. S08 form answers and S09 data views are separate canonical stores; neither is a prerequisite for an independent donation checkout. S10 may compose the registered payment UI only after its manual action is qualified.
- **Binding contracts:** A2/A4 one-owner commands; U1–U12 approved Particle presentation; H5/H6/L2–L4 revision, exact retry and uncertain-outcome recovery; P2 server-derived actor, organization and source scope; P3 separate platform-credit accounting; O7 published projection; E1/E2/E7/E8 acceptance. A public action may request checkout but never authorizes a charge, fund transfer, Stripe credential or connected-account change itself.
- **Usable outcome:** an authorized organization owner connects or reconnects **their existing Stripe account** through a supported account-connection path, sees whether it is able to accept charges and receive payouts, and enables a reviewed **Donate** or **Subscribe** action on the organization profile, a fundraiser or selected public page. Separately, where appropriate, an organization without a suitable connected account can complete a newly created account’s Stripe-hosted or embedded onboarding. A donor can make a one-time payment or authorize a recurring contribution; the organization sees independently verified payment/subscription states, refunds and disputes. The donor can manage or cancel the recurring arrangement through the permitted account-scoped Stripe-owned or qualified platform path. No successful payment is inferred from returning to the website.
- **Owners:** inspect current Stripe Connect/OAuth/onboarding, organization settings, transaction/finance, webhook, billing, public-profile, publication and donation/action components before assigning source files. Keep a single existing server-side Stripe owner; distinguish the **Coach House customer account** (platform subscriptions/AI credits) from each **organization connected account** and its donors. Preserve existing account IDs, keys, webhook identities, and test/live separation.
- **Work:**
  1. **Inspect and reuse; classify account API generation.** Inspect and record actual account connection modes (existing-account OAuth, account creation plus Connect Onboarding, embedded onboarding), Accounts v1 `Account`/controller properties versus Accounts v2 configurations/responsibilities, connection callback/state, account ownership, permissions, credential storage, Dashboard links, subscription/product/price/customer owners, webhook endpoints/scopes, disconnect/reconnect and existing tests. Classify each capability as inspected/working, incomplete or unavailable. **Record the Stripe API version and namespace used for each call, account-read, webhook, and object writer**; don't equate a v2 `Account` identity with permission to use every v2 endpoint. Accounts v2 offers `merchant`, `customer` and `recipient` configurations, but some flows still require Accounts v1 (including OAuth). Some v1 endpoints accept v2 account IDs; verify the specific endpoint, request and response mapping. Stripe discourages indefinitely operating dual Accounts API versions; document a bounded compatibility/migration decision only if the existing code requires one. No forced v1-to-v2 migration, parallel account creation, secret-key collection, credential sharing or speculative integration rewrite.
  2. **Existing-account connection versus new-account onboarding; readiness.** Treat these as **different supported paths**, not interchangeable mechanisms:
     - **Connect an existing Stripe account:** preserve the inspected authorized OAuth/Standard integration if it is the working path. OAuth authentication is an **Accounts v1** capability and still has limits: a platform OAuth connection may require a separate Standard account when the intended account is controlled by another platform. Validate `state`, registered redirect URI, exact returned account and reconnection; never imply every pre-existing account is attachable. Do not replace OAuth with an Account Link expecting it to attach an arbitrary pre-existing account.
     - **Create/onboard a connected account when necessary:** current SaaS setup uses **Accounts v2** where supported; create/configure the account with the correct Dashboard, `merchant` capability, fee/loss responsibility and onboarding owner, then use **Stripe-hosted** or **embedded Connect Onboarding** to collect requirements. Stripe-hosted onboarding uses a short-lived/single-use Account Link with server-generated `return_url` and `refresh_url`; a return does not prove verification. Retain the existing Accounts v1 path if the product/integration requires it. Do not create a duplicate Stripe account for an organization already properly connected.
     - **Shared readiness gate:** require explicit organization-owner authority for binding/rebinding; derive actor, organization and test/live environment server-side; check current Stripe account identity, payment/payout capabilities and requirements before allowing checkout. Model requirements-due, restricted, disabled, disconnected, expired authorization and reauthorization states. Preserve existing encrypted credentials where applicable; never request organization secret keys. A generic Edit/Manage permission cannot change Stripe binding, payout settings or finance responsibility.
  3. **Routing, custody and fees — explicit product decision before enabling charges.** Compare **direct charges on the organization’s account** against destination charges / separate charges and transfers. Record merchant of record, settlement/payout destination, Stripe processing and Connect fees, liability for negative balances/refunds/disputes, statement descriptor and whether Coach House takes any application fee. For existing-account SaaS and full-Dashboard connected accounts, direct charges are the first option to qualify. Stripe's SaaS **Stripe-owned pricing** arrangement normally has the connected merchant cover Stripe fees and negative-balance liability; a **buy-rate** arrangement moves fee/loss responsibility to the platform under its chosen terms. With Accounts v2, inspect `defaults.responsibilities.fees_collector` and `losses_collector`, and note that they cannot be changed after adding the Merchant configuration; confirm the corresponding Accounts v1 controller settings when applicable. Account ownership, Dashboard type and chosen charge model determine valid fees and liability. Never silently change an existing account's economics or default to Coach House receiving/holding charitable funds. Display the actual donation amount, any separately elected platform contribution/fee, recurring frequency and payee before confirmation; no hidden tips, fees or subscriptions.
  4. **One-time and campaign payments.** Reuse Stripe-hosted Checkout or the existing qualified payment surface. Create sessions **server-side in the account context required by the chosen charge model**; bind organization/account/campaign, valid amount, currency, idempotency and bounded metadata. Under direct charges, payment objects and Checkout sessions belong to the **connected account**, not the platform; requests and later readbacks use that connected-account context. Support optional fundraiser targets/dates and verified totals; distinguish authorized/processing/paid/refunded/disputed amounts. A fundraiser cannot mutate the canonical payments ledger by editing a displayed total. Public copies use a reviewed, authorized action specification; private Stripe credentials and unrelated donor data never enter public snapshots or AI prompts.
  5. **Recurring organization support and exact Stripe object ownership.** Implement a distinct **Subscribe** / recurring-donation flow through Stripe Billing. For **direct-charge subscriptions**, create and read **Products/Prices, donor Customers, Checkout sessions, Subscriptions and invoices in the same connected-account context**, using the account's Stripe authentication/header; never reuse a platform Price or platform Customer merely because an ID was cached. For destination-charge subscriptions, explicitly document the **platform-owned** objects and transfer/`on_behalf_of` behavior selected in step 3. Persist only minimal `{organization, environment, connectedAccount, customer, product, price, subscription, invoice, frequency}` references; validate every lookup against that account/environment. Handle incomplete, active, past-due, unpaid, canceled, renewed and failed-invoice states via independently verified provider reads.
     - **Management restrictions:** Stripe says a platform **cannot update/cancel a subscription created by another platform**, and only connected accounts with the **full Stripe Dashboard** can directly manage their customers' subscriptions; otherwise the platform must supply an authorized supported management path. Donor portal links/cancel actions must be created in the correct Stripe account context and must be independently tested; an account-agnostic platform billing portal is not a universal fallback. Subscription cancellation is distinct from canceled renewal/invoice settlement. **Disconnect does not automatically cancel recurring subscriptions**. Explicitly select continued billing versus authorized termination, customer notification and recovery when the original account can no longer be acted on. Coach House's own platform subscription and AI-credit products remain separate financial products.
  6. **Events, API-version scopes, reconciliation and recovery.** Verify Stripe webhook signatures against the raw request body and the correct **webhook signing secret**; distinguish platform events from Connect/connected-account events, endpoint/event API versions, relevant object ownership, test/live and sandbox identities. In Stripe's Connect event model, **v1 `account.updated` for connected accounts uses Connected accounts scope**, whereas **v2 `v2.core.account.*` for accounts represented in the platform uses Your account scope**; the same v2 account can yield events in both versions/scopes. **Direct-charge payment events** are connected-account events with an `account` identifier; fetch those Stripe objects as the identified connected account. Register the exact required event families under each scope, not a catch-all endpoint that assumes uniform payload shapes. Stripe notes that a production webhook URL may receive both live and test events, so inspect `livemode`; sandbox webhooks need their own endpoints. Persist durable webhook event/underlying payment/invoice/subscription identities, version and account scope; handle duplicates, delay, reordering and separate event IDs about the same payment without cross-org or double-credit outcomes. Re-fetch authoritative payment, invoice, subscription, capability and payout state as needed; verify settlement before marking paid or issuing an acknowledgment. Reconcile failures, refunds, disputes, reversals, fee adjustments and payout/transfer outcomes according to the charge model. A return URL, callback, webhook receipt or account ID alone never establishes success.
  7. **Privacy, records and closure.** Store only payment identifiers, amounts, currencies, status, minimal donor/receipt references and necessary audit data under the existing finance owner; do not persist card numbers, payment secrets, unnecessary donor identity, or Stripe customer records in board JSON. Separate Stripe's payment receipt from any organization-issued charitable acknowledgment; confirm nonprofit eligibility and any required tax-deductibility wording before labeling a payment tax-deductible. Define donor visibility and fundraising totals without exposing private donor data. Disconnect, organization closure and account deletion must **immediately disable new checkout** and revoke app authority, then reconcile existing recurring contributions, unpaid invoices, outstanding refunds/disputes, negative balances and retention obligations. **Stripe subscriptions survive account disconnection unless explicitly canceled**; a disconnection is not proof Coach House still has API authority to cancel them. Before closure enablement, define which party is able to cancel/change them, whether recurring donations continue, how donors are notified and what donor-facing self-service path remains. Never delete another party's Stripe records or silently cancel provider contracts.
- **Completion:** an organization can connect an existing Stripe account through an actually supported existing-account path, verify readiness, and publish a reviewed Donate/Subscribe action; an organization without a suitable connected account can complete the separately selected onboarding path. Test one-time and recurring transactions in Stripe test/sandbox mode and independently reconcile results. Demonstrate that every direct-charge session, donor Customer, Price, Subscription, invoice and cancellation/portal action is scoped to the **correct connected account**, and that selected destination-charge objects follow their explicit platform context. Verify actual connection limitations, Accounts v1 OAuth versus v2 onboarding, API-version compatibility, immutable fee/loss responsibilities, Dashboard restrictions, managed versus third-party subscriptions and behavior following disconnect. Test separate organizations, test/live and sandbox isolation, signed **Your account** versus **Connected accounts** webhooks, v1 versus v2 account events, cross-tenant denial, capability loss, stale callbacks, duplicate/out-of-order webhooks, delayed confirmation, exact checkout retry, failed invoice, payment failure, refund, dispute, canceled subscription, continuing subscription after disconnect, campaign totals, mobile/keyboard public checkout and closure fences. Current-revision hosted checks and authorized live activation are separate release gates.
- **Decision boundary:** select (a) charge/merchant-of-record and Stripe-owned versus buy-rate responsibility model, (b) platform fee/tip policy, (c) supported donation currencies/minimums and recurring frequencies, (d) qualifying nonprofit and acknowledgment rules, (e) disconnect/closure handling for recurring donor payments and customer communication, (f) the existing-account connection and any new-account onboarding path actually supported in this codebase, (g) whether/how an existing Accounts v1 integration interoperates with Accounts v2 or requires a separately approved migration, and (h) donor self-service versus platform-managed subscription cancellation under the actual Dashboard/account type. Record these as scoped decisions when inspected source requires them; none is already approved merely by this follow-up.
- **Limit:** no bespoke payment processor, stored card data, general-purpose wallet, pooled charitable custody, multi-beneficiary split checkout, automatic fundraiser execution, organization banking controls for invited editors or rewrite of S05 billing. Start with the smallest existing-account connection → one-time contribution → recurring contribution path and expand only after each canonical command, permission and recovery boundary passes. No provider/customer mutation, live charge, deployment or SHIP action is authorized by this document.

### Starting, overlapping and closing packets

1. **Start S01 only after the complete plan is approved and implementation authorized.** Its first checkpoint is the usable manual objective/plan/note interaction and shared contract—not an infrastructure-only registry PR declared finished.
2. **Apply settled decisions; qualify unknowns.** S03 applies section 4's approved D2 calculation/completion rules and fixtures; S06/S07 apply approved D5 and permission presets. S08 applies approved immediate submission, familiar form controls, form-collaborator response editing and 30-day closure; source/retention qualification precedes public intake. S05 owns final measured tariff quantities before customer billing; monthly/carryover/refund behavior is approved. Source adapter and processing qualification are engineering gates, not requests to reapprove the chosen presets/provider. See the boundary table below; no policy gap silently blocks unrelated planning.
3. **Overlap only stable interfaces.** Navigation can progress with a fixed membership contract; publication/intake can progress independently of AI; context work can progress independently of animation. Keep one owner for shared registry/schema/writer edits. Do not dispatch multiple agents into the same mutable contract. This describes possible execution, not a request to launch agents now.
4. **Close by behavior and evidence.** Update the one inventory/checkpoint with actual outcomes and unresolved checks, then mirror the document at a usable boundary. Do not call a packet done for file count, elapsed time, screenshots or schema-only success. If existing code already passes, close the requirement with evidence rather than rebuilding it.

## 10. Product behavior and proof

> **[VERIFY]** E1–E8 are required acceptance contracts, not passing results. Section 1 remains the implementation inventory; section 15 owns receipts and decisions. Reuse valid receipts when their code, environment and assertion scope are unchanged. No named organizational workflow defines MVP success.
>
> **[NOTE]** Test only enabled capabilities and their dependencies. Mentioning formulas, expiring links, external actions or retained memory does not add them to MVP. D2–D6 remain explicit boundaries. A capability with an unresolved required policy cannot be advertised as ready.

#### E1. Observable product behavior

The primary output is the useful board or working artifact. Chat supplies requests, necessary clarification and concise status. A generated description of a form, table or plan is not the corresponding functional output.

| Contract | User interaction | Observable acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| O1/O2: objective and plan | Describe an objective in the scoped composer; review the proposed plan; apply permitted changes | The scope and processing route are visible. A validated editable preview appears. Preview, saved proposal and accepted plan are distinguishable. Canonical readback and reload match the accepted change; no fabricated people, dates or evidence. Blank-board generation must work before that entry point is advertised. |
| O1/O2: focused revision | Select a plan/item and request a change | Review identifies additions, updates, removals and affected relationships. Unmentioned records, memberships, completed work, drafts and manual geometry remain unchanged. Owner acceptance changes only approved scope. A member's saved proposal does not become an accepted plan. |
| O1/O8: navigation | Select, expand, edit, traverse and return | Ordinary canvas click selects. Explicit controls expand/edit. A plan-list item focuses its existing placement. Escape closes the active surface and restores focus without losing drafts. Optional walkthrough uses the same navigation and does not write plan state. |
| O3: document | Edit a supported source through its existing editor | Save uses the source's canonical writer and revision. Another authorized reader sees the change. Read-only imports remain read-only; an attractive preview cannot imply write support. |
| O4/O5: form and intake | Edit a definition; publish an allowed form; submit; review privately | Preview submits nothing. Real intake binds the published form version, accepts approved fields, persists one submission and returns its receipt. Form creators/managers/editors see responses and can correct answer cells; unrelated viewers cannot. Definition changes do not reinterpret previous submissions, and submit retries do not undo corrections. |
| O6: data view | Ask for supported data; inspect, save and edit allowed cells | Rows match a canonical query with declared filters, ordering and pagination. Save preserves the view definition. A cell edit calls its registered source writer. Read-only technical fields stay read-only; authorized form collaborators can correct answer cells with conflict handling and change metadata. No response table is claimed complete before real intake exists. |
| O7: share | Select content; preview audience; publish; open mobile link; revoke | The page shows the organization and selected safe projections in explicit reading order. No unselected fields, private assets or edit authority leak. Named-canvas publication reads the intended canvas. After revocation, new authorized checks deny access; already downloaded copies cannot be recalled. |
| All: failure and recovery | Interrupt, lose connection, retry or encounter a conflict | Preserve recoverable drafts, report which operation is uncertain, reconcile its receipt before retrying and never show false success. A fresh reload reads canonical saved state. Unsupported operations remain unavailable with a short explanation and supported alternative where one exists. |

For each enabled output, account for creation, empty state, populated state, edit/save, reload, permission loss and recoverable failure through current applicable evidence. Prove common behavior once at its shared owner, then verify each variant’s actual wiring and unique behavior; do not duplicate the full shared suite for every variant. Distinct adapters, permission boundaries and persistence destinations still require their own evidence. For non-editable projections, prove that mutation controls and write authority are absent. Test relevant connections between outputs; isolated component success does not prove integration.

#### E2. Deterministic invariants

These are binary checks against application state, authorization and tool dispatch. All applicable checks must pass; a good-looking plan or high average model score cannot compensate for a failure.

| Boundary | Required fixture and independent assertion |
| --- | --- |
| Identity and scope | Two organizations, multiple users and named canvases; forged identifiers, revoked membership and stale access. Read/return/write/publication paths recheck authority. Denied results disclose no unauthorized existence or content. |
| Infrastructure migration and existing data | Reconcile affected files/bytes/versions, documents, notes, responses, canvas/plans/relationships, permissions and provider references before/after; verify stable identities, compatible readers/writers and usable recovery for the exact change. Reject unexplained loss, overwrite, orphaning, disconnection or access widening; unknown Storage objects remain untouched. Reuse unchanged proof; test the changed contract and critical preservation invariants. |
| Record versus placement | One record in two plans/placements. A canonical content edit updates the shared record; contextual membership and view state stay local. Removing membership does not delete a referenced record. |
| Revisions and concurrency | Two clients edit the same source; change source after preview and before apply. Stale writes conflict visibly; valid independent edits survive. Multi-owner results report each committed/failed effect without claiming global atomicity. |
| Proposal and application | Stage, reject and accept the same proposal. Pending storage may create proposed Particles as H2 specifies; it must not silently change accepted membership. Rejection cannot erase shared records. Duplicate acceptance returns its receipt or an explicit conflict without another effect. |
| Retry and interruption | Disconnect before and after canonical commit, cancel during a tool call, replay same request, reuse its ID with a different payload, exceed receipt retention. Verify effect and settlement counts from the canonical ledger. Unknown outcome requires reconciliation, not blind replay. |
| Typed boundaries | Invalid schema versions/types, temporary or nonexistent IDs, illegal transitions and unsupported adapters. Reject before executable rendering or mutation. TypeScript success alone does not prove runtime validation. |
| Bounds and abuse | Exactly 250/500 graph limits and cap+1, cycles where forbidden, missing endpoints, oversized context, malformed files and exhausted run/tool budgets. Fail without partial graph mutation or draft loss; conditional formula support also rejects arbitrary execution and unbounded expressions. |
| Disclosure and injection | Hostile instructions in documents, retrieved pages, tool results and output markup. Inspect actual provider/tool payloads and rendered DOM. External queries contain only authorized disclosure; unsafe HTML/URLs cannot execute. A prompt saying “keep private” is not enforcement. |
| Publication and intake | Tampered/revoked tokens, stale snapshots, cross-page assets, unpublished fields, extra submission fields and duplicate submits. Read actual public projections and private stored submissions. Expiry is checked only if supported; a public bearer token never grants edit access. |
| Collaboration and view state | Another user's mutation during expand/collapse, traversal and layout. Personal camera/selection/expansion changes do not overwrite shared state. Preserve manual/locked positions; temporary layout restoration cannot undo newer movements. |

Fixtures assert both the intended change and preservation of unrelated state. Expected state comes from fixture authors, canonical source reads and deterministic calculations—not the generating model's account of what it did.

#### E3. AI quality rubric

Evaluate schema validity separately from usefulness. Score each dimension **0: unusable**, **1: needs material correction**, **2: usable with ordinary editing**. “Ordinary editing” changes preference or detail; repairing wrong authority, invented facts, missing essential outputs or a structurally unusable plan is material correction.

| Dimension | A score of 2 requires |
| --- | --- |
| Outcome fit | Addresses the stated objective and constraints with a compact, coherent plan; avoids unrelated work and mandatory invented milestones. |
| Working outputs | Chooses supported capabilities and makes the needed artifact editable/usable; does not substitute prose for an artifact or claim unavailable functions. |
| Dependencies and decisions | Captures necessary order, parallel work and unresolved decisions without manufacturing dependencies or blocking questions. |
| Grounding and uncertainty | Uses authorized relevant sources, distinguishes inference/unknowns from facts, and links evidence to claims. Current permission and source revision remain checkable. |
| Revision fidelity | Performs the requested change, reuses existing work and preserves unrelated accepted work, identities and relationships. |
| Presentation | Shows the result on the board with concise labels and actionable status; no unsolicited essay, redundant summary, unexplained duplicates or needless layers. |
| Tool efficiency | Retrieves enough relevant evidence with bounded targeted calls, avoids repeated unchanged reads and stops when the requested result is ready or a real blocker remains. |

Forbidden tool use, unauthorized disclosure, invented completion of an action, invalid persisted state or silent overwrite is a hard failure regardless of rubric score. For sparse context, an honest useful partial plan can outperform an exhaustive fabricated plan. Do not force citations for proposed ideas; do require support for claims presented as known organizational facts.

**[ANSWERED] Qualification procedure:** establish a baseline on the current supported route, calibrate rubric examples with a product reviewer, then freeze per-capability quality floors and latency/cost ceilings before comparing candidates. Record both absolute usability and regression against baseline. Do not claim release readiness while those thresholds are unset or measured only on prompt-tuning examples. This is a bounded evaluation prerequisite, not a new product-discovery exercise or a demand for another provider.

#### E4. Evaluation set and grading

**Executable evidence requirement (November5):** within existing acceptance/browser/database seams, maintain a versioned case manifest, deterministic graders, a separately authorized bounded live-provider runner, a held-out qualification partition and a machine-readable result receipt. Each receipt includes case/configuration revisions, attempts including failures, actual usage/cost, timing stages, semantic preservation checks and human-calibrated usefulness/grounding scores. Derive reports from these receipts, not a second billing ledger. No new vendor or automatic paid CI job is required. [AI integration completion contract — November5](#ai-integration-completion-contract--november5) milestone5 owns final per-capability release decisions; baseline and affected regression evaluation begin with the first implementation slice.

**Cadence for S04/S05/S10/S11:** routine development uses a small fixed deterministic smoke set with mocked provider/tool outputs for affected parsing, orchestration and rendering behavior. This proves mechanics, not live planning quality. Run broader affected quality/retrieval cases when model/configuration, prompts/skills, tools, retrieval or planning logic changes; perform representative integration qualification before release. Reuse valid qualification for unchanged capabilities. Repeated stochastic and held-out trials below apply to qualification, not every edit or packet. Live evaluation still requires authorized data, route and spending budget. No automatic paid evaluation follows from a code change.

Use a versioned suite organized by capabilities, not a single “golden journey.” Include new objective generation, revision, supported output construction, retrieval, collaboration and sharing where enabled. Vary sparse/rich/conflicting context, existing reusable work, scale, permission role, source format and interruption point. Include different organizational objectives as inputs without turning any one into scope.

Each case records: request; authorized starting state; source revisions; enabled tools and policies; expected invariants; acceptable result properties; forbidden effects; required evidence; and applicable O/H/K/E identifiers. Fix time, locale and tool responses for deterministic cases. Use synthetic or authorized de-identified records for reusable fixtures; do not copy production personal data or credentials into tests/traces.

- Separate development cases from held-out qualification cases. Keep adversarial and regression cases after a failure is fixed. A case added to training/prompt-tuning ceases to be held-out evidence.
- Code graders check schema, permissions, graph invariants, arithmetic, source identity, preservation and final state. Test retrieval against curated relevant sources, including missed evidence and incomplete coverage; finding one valid source does not prove recall.
- Human-calibrated model graders may assist subjective usefulness assessments. They receive only authorized, minimized evidence; their output is neither an access decision nor sole proof of correctness. Spot-check disagreement and failures against human review. Do not ask the generating run to certify itself.
- Repeat stochastic cases with the same inputs/configuration. Record every attempt, including refusals, timeouts and failures. Report per-capability/per-route results and sample sizes; averages cannot hide a failing capability or discarded runs. One successful run is demonstration, not reliability evidence.
- A retry that eventually succeeds still counts its first failure, total latency, calls and cost. Measure first-attempt usability separately from recovery. Parallel agents or extra judgments must show benefit against added cost/latency before adoption.

This follows [OpenAI agent evaluations](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agent-evals) for repeatable datasets and trace inspection, and [Anthropic agent evaluation guidance](https://www.anthropic.com/research/demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents) for grading outcomes, repeated trials and calibrated evaluators. These sources guide the method; Coach House's invariants and qualification thresholds remain product-owned.

#### E5. Interaction and performance measurement

Measure the actual implementation, not a screenshot or model response alone. During development, measure affected interactions and reuse valid shared-surface evidence; representative integrated qualification remains required before release. Straightforward spacing/copy/style changes use focused inspection and existing accessibility/baseline checks, not new tests that merely mirror markup. Add a regression test when changed behavior or a concrete recurring failure warrants it; required repository visual baselines still apply. Use representative mobile and desktop viewports, keyboard-only operation, screen-reader semantics, reduced motion, slow network and production-like builds. Record device, viewport, build mode, dataset size and network conditions. A fixture's speed cannot establish the full app's speed.

| Measurement | Acceptance rule |
| --- | --- |
| Immediate feedback | Instrument user input to visible acknowledgement; section 5 targets ≤100 ms, with visible pending feedback by 400 ms when work continues. Report p50/p95 and failures. Do not relabel a loading shimmer as a useful AI result. |
| AI timing | Record request admission, first useful validated preview, terminal generation, proposal save and canonical apply separately. H7's timeout is an upper work bound, not a usability promise. Benchmark quality alongside latency and cost. |
| Save and recovery | Measure save-to-confirmed-readback and failure-to-recoverable-state. Successful optimistic display does not stop the persistence clock. Count timeouts and unknown outcomes separately from successful latency. |
| Animation | Section 5's 160–240 ms transition target and existing camera behavior remain distinct. Interaction stays interruptible; reduced motion preserves meaning without required movement. Pending animation cannot hide a save failure or move focus unexpectedly. |
| Layout and traversal | Exercise small, typical and near-cap graphs. Expanded bounds include assignments. No overlap makes required controls unreachable; manual/locked geometry and reading order survive navigation. Public mobile layout does not depend on canvas coordinates. |
| Accessibility | Touch targets ≥44×44 CSS px; desktop actions follow the shared 28px minimum and U3 focus/hit-region rules; visible focus, labeled status not color alone, usable keyboard alternatives to dragging, no focus traps and preserved drafts on dismissal. Test status announcements and menus in the actual interaction. |

For latency/cost reports, show sample count, success denominator, failures, cache conditions and provider configuration. Performance optimizations must preserve the same E2 correctness checks. Existing limits remain until measured evidence and a compatible schema/migration change justify changing them.

A bounded usability check asks an intended user to generate, locate, edit, recover and share an enabled output without developer guidance. Observe task completion, assistance, mistaken expectations and lost work; do not require screenshot approval as a substitute. Use different objectives; intake review is tested when intake is enabled. A persistent misunderstanding about save, proposal or publication state is a product defect, not merely a copy preference.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `tests/acceptance/workspace-research-provider.test.ts` | Mocked provider/tool-loop behavior, declared calls, budget handling and invalid evidence rejection | Real provider quality, hosted tool behavior, live disclosure containment or actual billing |
| `tests/acceptance/workspace-sharing-database.test.ts` | Transaction/concurrency behavior against a configured test database | A run without `WORKSPACE_SHARING_TEST_DATABASE_URL` skips this suite; skipped is not passing database evidence |

| O1–O8/H10/K9 source and test pointers | Existing owners and focused seams to extend rather than duplicate | Source inspection is not execution; reference-pack tests are not Coach House integration proof |

Use existing Vitest acceptance projects, relevant database/RLS suites and browser seams for affected behavior. Add full-app checks only where fixture tests cannot prove the required boundary. A live AI qualification uses authorized non-production data, the approved route and a capped budget; it must not send messages, publish or charge an unapproved funding source as incidental evaluation.

Keep existing CI guardrails. During development, run focused checks; use the complete local quality suite only when explicitly requested or diagnosing a concrete CI failure. When tests change, maintain the existing acceptance manifest. Intended visual changes follow repository baseline rules; never weaken thresholds to make a regression pass. None of these runtime checks is needed merely to validate this documentation edit.

#### E7. Evidence receipt

Store a concise receipt in the existing owner checkpoint, not a new tracking system. Include:

- Requirement IDs and enabled capability/route; code commit plus dirty-patch identifier when relevant; schema, prompt/skill, tool registry, fixture and evaluator versions.
- Environment and test command; date; pass/fail/skip counts and reasons; expected versus observed state; sanitized trace/artifact pointers. Never include credentials, bearer tokens, hidden reasoning or unnecessary personal data.
- For AI runs: actual provider/model/configuration, attempt count, tool calls, usage/cost certainty, tariff version, per-dimension scores and unresolved limitations. Unknown usage is unknown, not zero.
- For effects: independently read canonical IDs/revisions/receipts and verify unrelated-state preservation. Check both allowed and denied identities. The same mocked response supplying both action and verification is not independent persistence evidence.
- Which gates remain: local, hosted CI, review, deployment, live provider and live product acceptance. Reuse receipts while their claims remain valid. Relevant changes to code, tests, schemas, configuration, dependencies, environment or observed failures invalidate affected evidence; unrelated edits alone do not. Mandatory current-revision release checks still rerun as required. Reference the existing receipt instead of copying it; failed, skipped and inconclusive checks cannot become passing evidence through reuse.

#### E8. Release interpretation

Complete-plan approval precedes application implementation; a completed documentation pass does not authorize it. Section 9 remains the sole dependency sequence. An enabled capability is ready only when its output contract, applicable U1–U12 UI rules, required D decisions, applicable deterministic checks, qualified AI behavior where used, integrated interaction and recovery are evidenced. Block the failing capability or repair it; do not average safety failures away or claim the full MVP by silently removing required scope.

Required hosted `quality` and branch-protection checks must pass for the current PR revision. Review, deployment and live acceptance remain separate; passing local tests does not authorize or prove them. Migration/backward-compatibility, pre/post reconciliation and verified recovery of affected records, stored bytes, references and permissions are mandatory before releasing changed infrastructure or stored contracts, under the November11 preservation amendment. An unexplained mismatch or unverified recovery blocks that migration/cutover. Deferred historical-restore infrastructure and self-service closure remain outside launch scope; they do not excuse unsafe migrations or block unrelated qualified AI delivery. Non-destructive disabling of an AI route must preserve existing manually editable work.

**Acceptance checkpoint:** product behavior, evaluation method and evidence boundaries are approved. No new runtime pass results or quality baselines are claimed. D3/D4 require source/retention qualification; D6 requires measured tariff quantities; numerical AI qualification thresholds need measured baselines. Section 9 S01–S11 now binds these acceptance IDs to execution packets under the existing dependency order.

## 13. Concrete system rules strengthened by the reference

> **[PROPOSED]** These rules strengthen the target contract; they are not implemented merely by being written. The optional walkthrough requirement is user-approved; its detailed interaction defaults below remain recommendations.

### Identity, projection and evidence

The saved graph is not the rendered graph. Existing records and plan memberships produce view cards; grouping, search, previews and outside-scope connectors are projections.

| Contract | Required fields / invariant |
| --- | --- |
| Record reference | Organization/source owner + stable record ID + kind + source revision; server resolves access |
| Plan membership | Plan ID + record/Particle reference + contextual assignment/order; same source may appear in other plans |
| View card | Scope/placement identity + canonical reference + display role (`record`, `group`, `connector`); no independent authority |
| View connection | Stable key + projected endpoints + semantic kind/direction + supporting raw relationship IDs + provenance |
| Evidence | Source identity/revision + locator + basis (`source`, `authored`, `inferred`) + extraction completeness; claims bind to their evidence |
| View request | Authorized scope + view kind + selected/context references + source/graph revisions + request identity |
| UI result | Discriminated result kind + validated target/configuration + provenance + permitted actions + truthful persistence status |

These are adapter requirements, not a replacement database schema. Preserve current IDs, public URLs and saved content. Build one Zod source of truth for each application boundary and infer TypeScript types; avoid manually maintaining competing JSON Schema and TypeScript definitions.

Group only compatible relationships. Retain all supporting raw links and evidence; do not merge a proposal into accepted work or an inferred connection into an established prerequisite. Counts deduplicate canonical records within their stated scope and exclude unauthorized records **before** projection. A hidden/private record cannot leak through a connector label, count, path, search result or AI context.

A visual route means connection, not causation or execution. Grouped edges cannot be directly deleted as though they were one stored edge: resolve their underlying relationships and preview the exact change. Off-board proxies reveal the authorized source location and do not create extra records, assignments or completion units.

### Typed AI results that show work

Keep the current bounded research generation and semantic validation. Add the shared result envelope around those owners rather than replacing them with the pack's `Answer` format.

- Distinguish existing references from newly proposed items. New items use validated local keys; the application assigns/preserves IDs when committing. Unknown existing references fail closed.
- Bind output to run, organization, selected plan, relevant graph/source revisions and capability version. A graph revision alone does not prove a document, person or permission is unchanged.
- A read-only answer projects authorized existing information. An edit result previews typed commands. Neither may silently execute the other.
- Required affected items remain visible or reachable with an explicit omission indicator. Never truncate away a decision outcome, prerequisite or required review target to meet a card cap.
- Show the plan/table/diff. Default status is zero or one sentence; new generated titles usually 3–5 words; one clarification when necessary. Preserve exact names, facts, dates and user wording. No automatic three-question follow-up panel.
- Stop cancels the identified run. Late results cannot replace newer work or clear another run's pending state. Preserve the prompt, selected context and unsaved manual work.

### Optional guided walkthrough — approved

> **[ANSWERED]** Include optional walkthroughs, per the user's October 28 reply. **[NEEDS BUILD]** Integrate orchestration/return state with existing focus controls. No separate learning system or completion side effect is authorized.

Provide one contextual “Walk through” action for a plan. Direct exploration remains available; no automatic tour or added permanent toolbar.

1. Start from the selected accepted plan or clearly labeled proposal. Capture return scope, camera, selection and keyboard focus. Choose the current plan order/selected route; do not silently decide an unresolved branch.
2. Next/Back focuses an existing visible item using the current camera controller. Show its title, owner where available, and at most one short explanation of purpose or dependency. “Why” reveals sources/details only when requested.
3. An actual connection carries its direction/evidence. A narrative jump is a navigation transition, never a fabricated dependency or permanently saved edge. Alternative paths remain labeled as alternatives.
4. A sequence refers to existing plan membership; it does not turn every document, person or form into a task. Advancing never marks work done, accepts a proposal, changes assignments, submits a form, sends a message, or awards Accelerator completion.
5. Exit restores the prior view/focus. Navigation respects dirty-editor guards. A deleted/inaccessible target gets an explicit unavailable state and safe next/back/exit choices; never show stale restricted content.
6. Bind generated narration to plan and source revisions. A changed plan invalidates affected narration. Cached/session narration is sufficient initially; do not introduce a separately editable “flow” database just to navigate a plan.
7. Keyboard and touch have explicit Next/Back/Exit controls. Reduced motion changes focus immediately with static highlighting. Use a mobile list/stack where the graph is impractical. Displayed `2 of 6` measures navigation only.

### Navigation, layout and motion

Maintain one navigation history across overview, selected plan, item detail and temporary result view. Back returns to the actual prior context, not always the root. Search reveal and walkthrough focus use the same command; no independent camera owners.

Fit considers the live rectangles occupied by Objectives, Opportunities, composer, windows and walkthrough controls. Keep selected content reachable without zooming everything into illegibility. A focused plan projection can reduce visible detail without changing stored memberships or completion.

Use the existing ELK measured-layout pipeline. Include expanded content, assignments and action areas in bounds. A layout identity combines scope, graph/source revision, measurement key and sequence token. Stale success, failure and cleanup are all ignored. Preserve manual/locked positions; preview and accepted-state geometry are distinct. Do not run layout on every streamed token or keystroke.

Apply progressive disclosure to secondary text and metadata; keep titles, status meaning and focus legible. Do not copy the reference's numeric zoom thresholds without checking Coach House geometry. Keep separate visual channels for type, work status, proposal state, selection and focus; green must not mean both “recently changed” and “completed” without another distinguishing cue.

Refresh reconciles IDs and source revisions, preserves drafts and personal view state, and flags stale summaries. A failed analysis is not an empty/healthy result. Authored content is never overwritten by generated descriptions during refresh.

**Approval boundary:** the user approved the six recommended defaults and this planning work, not an already unseen final document or app implementation. A graph commit cannot stand in for a document save, form submission or publication transaction. - **[REQUIRED] Evidence:** assess capabilities and their combinations using varied objectives, including sparse context, existing work, conflicts and denied access. ### Composer context and Tools reorganization plan — November4

Status: resume from “Composer @ context and slash menu — November4” below. Step1 and planning-context selection/delivery are implemented on localhost:3153; document-edit references and steps3–5 remain (slash preset browsing/dismissal is implemented). This is the authoritative plan; the two existing spec mirrors remain exact copies.

#### Confirmed interaction model

| Surface | Purpose | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tools → Plugins | Existing integrations and connection controls | Connect/manage a plugin |
| Tools → Particles | Existing preset catalog and reusable particles, below Plugins | Configure/create/place a particle |
| Composer + and @ | The same AI context picker | Attach people, documents, plans, objectives or particles |
| Documents submenu | Workspace documents, Upload from computer, Google Drive | Select/upload authorized files into composer context |
| Composer / | Searchable creation commands | Add an Objective or supported particle/preset |
| Plain composer text | The existing AI planning/document request flow | Review/generate a proposal using explicit context |

Caleb explicitly confirmed that + is for AI context and includes computer upload and Google Drive submenu options. It no longer opens the particle library. Mentioning a person does not assign them, invite them, grant access or notify them. Context selection does not create or place particles. Slash creation uses the existing save pipeline and does not require a paid AI call.

#### Screenshot evidence and design notes

Available images inspected directly: `Screenshot 2026-11-04 at 12.24.28 PM.png` and `Screenshot 2026-11-04 at 12.24.37 PM.png` in Downloads (filenames contain a narrow space before PM). These are the two earlier ChatGPT composer screenshots. The latest request contains React Grab references but no additional image attachment. The available images do not show an open picker, submenu or slash menu. Computer/Drive submenu requirements are confirmed by Caleb's text; their exact screenshot styling remains unobserved.

1. A single broad rounded composer contains attachments, text and toolbar. There is no separate attachment panel outside it and no second prompt form.
2. The dark outer surface is lighter than the attached document card. The boundary is a subtle stroke; no prominent drop shadow is visible. Use Coach House theme tokens and the already requested shadow-free treatment.
3. The file card sits at the upper left inside the composer with consistent top/left inset. Text starts below the attachment area and aligns to the composer's left content edge.
4. The card has a preview region above its filename row. The preview is a restrained centered file outline, not a paragraph of explanatory text.
5. A small source/type mark precedes the filename at the lower left. The long filename truncates to one line. Preserve the complete accessible name and tooltip.
6. The first image has a quiet card border and no visible remove control. In the second, the border is stronger and a circular X appears overlapping the top-right corner. The images establish two visual states; they do not prove whether hover, focus or selection caused the difference.
7. The card's position and size, filename baseline, prompt and toolbar remain aligned between the two images. Removal affordances must be positioned without changing layout. Show removal on keyboard focus and always make it discoverable on touch; hover cannot be the only route.
8. The plus is leftmost in the bottom toolbar; submit is rightmost. Their alignment is independent of filename length and removal state.
9. The screenshot also contains a reasoning selector and microphone. They are reference context only, not requested Coach House features; do not add them.
10. The screenshot is a magnified capture with a tall composer. Copy its hierarchy and interaction, not literal screenshot dimensions. Coach House remains compact when empty and grows only when attachments or multiline text need space.
11. Attachment cards should be shallow, consistent, horizontally scrollable above the text on narrow screens, with a visible scroll affordance; avoid letting many cards create a tall vertical wall. People/plans/objectives/particles use smaller contextual chips with the same remove behavior rather than blank document previews.
12. Keep the dock anchored at the bottom. New content expands upward; suggestions, errors and proposal review open above the dock without moving the toolbar or canvas. No nested bordered prompt containers or explanatory copy blocks.
13. A photo/preview is used only when an existing safe preview is available. Document type/source icons and initials are fallbacks. Do not fetch arbitrary thumbnails or invent provider read success.
14. Light/dark treatment must match current menus and surfaces: left alignment, compact typography, restrained icons, thin borders, no default shadows, bounded menu height and 44px touch targets around smaller visual controls.

Pending visual evidence: the referenced open-menu/submenu screenshots. Their row ordering, spacing, labels, active states, submenu positioning and overflow behavior cannot be inferred from the two attachment screenshots. This plan defines those behaviors provisionally from the explicit request and existing Coach House conventions.

#### Tools consolidation

Use one Tools view with peer section headings **Plugins** then **Particles**. Retain Installed/Available as subordinate plugin groupings where populated. Preserve existing provider state, connection flows and permissions. Place the existing particle gallery below; retain preset configuration, image handling, drag-to-place, restore hidden particles, search and retained draft state. Avoid duplicating the gallery or copying its create logic.

Remove the separate visible Particles navigation entry. Normalize legacy `tab: particles` requests, saved navigation and tutorial/browse entry points to Tools with its Particles section focused or scrolled into view. Existing links must still land usefully. Top tabs already include Tools; the alternate drawer navigation and retained content still contain a separate particles branch and both must be handled. Preserve organization/Back transitions and fullscreen coverage.

Maintain one scroll surface and consistent section insets. A particle preset editor replaces the Tools body temporarily with Back to Tools, preserving plugin state, particle query and scroll position. Keep plugin-management controls out of the particle gallery itself; audit `ParticleLibrary.tools` to avoid duplicating existing canvas tools.

#### + and @ context picker

The + button opens a compact picker above the left side of the composer, labelled Add context. Root categories: People, Documents, Plans, Objectives, Particles. A search field searches readable records with category grouping. Empty query shows useful current-workspace items, not an unexplained blank area. Names remain primary; use a small type/source mark and only enough secondary context to distinguish duplicate names.

Documents offers **Workspace documents**, **Upload from computer…**, **Google Drive…**. The first leads to the existing document library search. Upload invokes a native multiple-file picker. Drive invokes the existing selected-file Google picker when connected and its existing connect/reconnect flow otherwise. Desktop submenus stay within the viewport; narrow screens replace the picker page with Back instead of stacking flyouts. Escape returns from a submenu first, then closes the picker and restores the original caret.

Typing @ at a token boundary opens the same picker and filters as the user types. Do not activate inside email addresses, pasted text, code or an IME composition. Selection replaces only the active @ query with a stable mention token and adds the matching context item; preserve the surrounding text and caret. + selection adds a context item without changing prompt text. De-duplicate the same canonical record across +, mentions and document/source aliases. Removing a context item also removes its linked mention token(s), leaving ordinary prose intact. Backspace adjacent to a mention selects/removes it predictably; plain pasted @names remain text unless resolved by the picker.

People context comes from readable People records and identifiable teammates, with record kind disambiguation where needed. Keep the team-only assignment eligibility rule separate. Plan references include canvas, objective and plan identity plus revision; a plan ID alone is insufficient. Objectives and particles default to the current board. Cross-board results, if offered by an existing authorized search, must show their board and retain that scope explicitly.

Arrow keys navigate results; Enter selects a result while the picker is open and never sends the prompt. Escape closes it. Tab maintains normal accessible focus behavior. Outside click dismisses suggestions without deleting text. Search is debounced, cancellable and scoped to the active organization/board; late results cannot leak into a switched workspace.

#### Attachments and AI context must work end to end

Represent selection as typed references, not visible labels pasted into the prompt: kind, organization/canvas scope as applicable, stable ID, compound plan identity and revision. Titles and avatars are display caches. The server resolves every reference with the authenticated actor and rechecks visibility, deletion/revocation and revision before reading and before applying generated changes. Do not accept client-supplied document bodies, arbitrary URLs, storage paths or provider tokens as authority.

Reuse existing uploaded-file and document authorization/storage readers. Upload a file through the bounded file-upload path, then attach the returned source reference; never put base64 files into a chat Server Action. Persist uploads in Documents using the existing durable source model; adding them to context does not also place them on the canvas. Removing a context card only removes that reference from the request. It does not delete a stored file or a Google Drive original.

Card states: uploading/preparing, ready, unavailable/error; show concise state only when actionable. Failed items retain the user's prompt and other selections. Retry only the failed upload/read preparation, without duplicating a successfully stored source. Block sending while a selected item is unresolved; let the user remove it or retry. Unsupported/metadata-only sources must be identified before generation, never represented as fully read files. Preserve existing file/type/byte and evidence limits; proposed initial context cap:10 unique items, subject to the existing request/evidence budget. Capacity failures identify the affected item rather than silently dropping context.

Existing AI research accepts prompt/target/skill but has no explicit context-reference collection. Extend the request, run fingerprint/idempotency data, source/evidence tracking and freshness checks together. Selected references must be resolved deterministically and supplied to the provider through the existing bounded evidence pipeline; keyword search alone is not enough to honor attachments. Recheck read access on retries and resumed requests. Preserve person-field restrictions and document partial-read/metadata-only coverage. External document content remains untrusted data, never tool instructions.

Drive-specific gap: the current knowledge loader excludes core documents with `driveSource` and searches uploaded organization files; attaching a Drive link does not currently establish AI-readable content. Add selected-file authorized content/export reading through the existing Google integration, with supported formats, bounded extraction and freshness checks. Reuse `pickGoogleDriveFiles`, connection and documents routes. Return selected references to the composer instead of relying only on the existing attach count and library refresh. A link-only or unsupported Drive file gets a precise unavailable/content-limited state; no fabricated read success.

The current Drive connect flow redirects to `/workspace/documents`. For composer use, preserve a bounded draft keyed to user/organization/board and return to the original workspace/composer after the existing validated OAuth return flow. Do not change OAuth scope or provider access rules merely for menu convenience. If local draft storage is unavailable, prevent silent draft loss during redirect. Cancellation and reconnect errors preserve text/context and focus.

Context does not choose a mutation target by implication. Mentioning a plan supplies context; it does not silently replace the current generation target. Existing document editing still requires an explicit writable editor target, distinct from reference documents. Retain review/apply, canonical revision guards, conflict recovery, credits/stop behavior and the existing staging20-call/$3 ceiling. No allowance reset or paid inference is authorized by this plan-writing slice.

#### / creation menu

Typing / at a token boundary opens a compact searchable command menu above the composer. Ignore slashes in URLs/paths and IME input. Source entries from the existing particle/preset registry so Tools and / stay consistent. Put Objective first, then existing supported particle/preset labels (including Resource, Notes, Checklist, Decision, Calendar/Event, People, Metric, Workflow, Finance, Form, Data view and Image where available); filter by current permissions and feature flags.

Selecting a basic command sets a visible command chip and title prompt in the same composer. It does not immediately create an empty record or call AI. Enter/Add commits through the existing authorized creation and placement path. Complex presets use their existing configuration editor through Tools with Back, while preserving the chat draft/context. Selecting or cancelling a command must not discard a composed AI request. Avoid a second chat input or a second particle-creation implementation.

Plain text continues to the existing AI review/planning flow. Explicit / commands select creation mode. Existing `create objective …` / `create resource …` strings can remain compatible aliases; remove the current hidden keyword routing that unexpectedly treats a normal AI sentence as a particle-library search. Tools owns library search. Preserve Enter/Shift+Enter behavior and prevent a menu selection from also submitting.

#### Implementation boundaries and sequence

1. **Tools consolidation, complete navigation slice.** Compose the current plugin panel and particle library under two headings; migrate old particle-tab requests; verify browse/configure/place, Back and retained drafts.
2. **Context selection plus actual AI delivery.** Add typed references, authorized search/read resolution, shared +/@ picker and draft state; wire people/documents/plans/objectives/particles into request/evidence/freshness. Ship this slice only when selected context affects the provider request and proposals, not when chips merely render.
3. **Computer and Drive documents.** Reuse upload/picker APIs; add bounded Drive content access and the missing selection result adapter; wire upload/preparation/retry/remove and OAuth draft return. Test successful content use and unavailable cases before claiming attachment support.
4. **Slash creation.** Reuse registry/create/save/layout paths; implement keyboard/caret parsing, mode selection, title/configuration, cancellation and preserved chat drafts.
5. **Integrated visual and behavior verification.** Validate the same stationary composer in empty, one/many contexts, upload pending/error, menu/submenu, long-name, mobile and dark/light states. Update the exact staging export only after the integrated checks; preserve production and current private environment/servers.

Main code owners: `ParticleComposer` (text/caret/menus/toolbar), `WorkspaceParticleComposerSlot` (composition/dispatch), `WorkspaceNewPlan` and `WorkspaceResearch` (request/context propagation), `WorkspaceAiComposer` (document target/reference separation), `research-types.ts` and server research/knowledge modules (authorized references/evidence), `workspace-drawer-content.tsx` and drawer navigation/request routing (Tools consolidation), `WorkspaceToolsPanel` and `ParticleLibrary` (retained section content), Documents upload/Drive hooks and `src/features/google-drive` (file selection/reading). Keep route files composition-only and reuse existing feature boundaries. Scope any new feature scaffold to a genuinely new feature; this reorganization primarily extends existing owners.

#### Acceptance evidence

- One Tools destination, Plugins above Particles; old browse links still work; no duplicate galleries or lost preset drafts.
- + and @ resolve the same identities. All five categories search correctly, duplicate names are distinguishable, and cross-workspace/stale responses are rejected.
- Actual provider-request tests prove selected documents and records are included, removed context is absent, and a mention does not mutate/assign/share anything.
- A computer upload over1MB stays outside the chat action payload; multi-file progress/failure/removal and source persistence are verified. Google Drive selection, cancellation/reconnect, revoked access, unsupported format and actual bounded content reading have independent evidence.
- Plan identities stay isolated across objectives/canvases. Removed/changed sources cannot be silently reused. Existing proposal application, conflict handling and credit ceiling remain enforced.
- / exposes supported commands, preserves draft/context when cancelled, creates exactly once on explicit submit, and keeps no dead creation paths.
- Chromium/WebKit: caret insertion/deletion, email/URL/IME exclusions, keyboard menus/submenus, focus return, touch targets, stationary toolbar, no accidental send, long filenames and constrained width. Screenshots verify light/dark and the remove-control geometry against supplied references.
- Reuse valid existing checks; add tests only for new parsing/state/authorization/persistence behavior. Run focused checks per completed slice; keep hosted quality/review and production release gates separate.

#### Alternatives considered

Recommended: one +/@ context system, a separate / command mode and one Tools library. This follows Caleb's confirmed destinations and reuses identity/selection logic. A single mixed context-and-create picker would save a component but mix attaching existing records with creating new ones. Keeping Particles as a separate panel and adding a Tools shortcut would reduce navigation edits but fail the requested consolidation. Neither alternative is the selected direction.

Remaining input: the open-picker/submenu screenshots for exact visual annotation. The functional destination of +, computer upload and Google Drive is confirmed; this visual gap does not require re-asking that decision.

#### AI integration completion contract — November5

**Status: user-approved operational-workspace scope, replacing the narrower first amendment.** One workspace to plan and do: connect organizational information and tools, answer using real data, create usable artifacts, perform authorized actions and continue working with the results on the canvas. This is the single active AI completion contract inside S04/S05/S08/S09/S10/S11; no second architecture or roadmap. It supersedes earlier blanket deferrals of explicit saved guidance, basic hybrid retrieval, a bounded decision integration and native form-to-Sheets delivery. Preserve the main thread's work, valid receipts and reviewed minimal interface. The external architecture handoff remains reference input, not execution authority.

**One system, explicit authorities:** extend the current capability registry, source readers/writers, conversation owner, authorization and credit ledger. Manual controls and AI operations use the same definitions and handlers. Source systems retain canonical records; the canvas presents authorized records/results and their actual actions. Search indexes, embeddings, caches and model judgments are derived support, never competing factual, permission, mutation or billing stores. Internal storage does not imply atomicity across external services; retain exact operation receipts and reconcile partial/unknown effects.

**Inspected implementation baseline (November5, not new acceptance):** AI SDK7.0.162/React4.0.166 chat transport, shadcn chat compositions and native OpenAI6.25.0 Responses are integrated. Retain current AG-UI non-chat and json-render/Apps SDK UI consumers without a replacement runtime. Existing catalog entries cover manual plans/notes/forms/data views; some AI bindings exist separately. The two model research tools are `search_workspace` and `read_workspace`; this is a current endpoint limitation, not the intended platform capability ceiling. At that inspection, history reconstructed run-linked prompts/summaries/references and capped turns at12. The later [durable chat history checkpoint](#durable-chat-history-implementation--november5) records persistence/paging and removal of that cap; The later [read-only reply checkpoint](#read-only-chat-replies-implementation--november5) records Answer/Clarify dispatch; live qualification remains open. Accepted-plan revision preserves identity but currently changes title/membership/connections, not saved note/document bodies. Connected-source/provider/hosted readiness must be verified individually; no Gmail or general external-write completion is claimed here.

**Non-negotiable user outcomes:**

- **Answer/Clarify:** retrieve current permitted data, explain the result and identify relevant source/date/range and unknowns. Answer-only turns do not create fake plans. Clarification does not hold a provider loop open. Use the approved P3 metered-turn rule: completed answers and clarifications consume usage regardless of subjective usefulness/topic; qualify the exact tariff/accounting before activation.
- **Propose:** construct the requested supported working artifact or precise revision, editable inside the existing chat/canvas flow. A note saying “create a form” is not a form; a filename is not read document content. Pending proposals can be discussed/refined without implicit acceptance; implement correct pending-proposal supersession through its existing owner.
- **Apply:** explicit user intent and required review invoke canonical handlers. Add/whole-plan drag/retry share effect identity. Sending, publication, event changes and destination writes require their specific authorization; generation never claims them completed before a confirmed receipt.
- **Continue:** reopened conversations and fresh chats retrieve relevant current facts, decisions and explicitly saved guidance. Users can inspect/edit/delete their permitted guidance and continue developing the same artifacts without duplication or unrelated changes.

**Required MVP integration surface:** each enabled source/action must be usable end to end, with real data and a reviewed canvas representation. These rows define outcomes, not an assertion that every adapter exists. Reuse working implementations first. Broad future catalog expansion, arbitrary providers and universal bidirectional sync are not implied.

| Capability/source | Required behavior and authority |
| --- | --- |
| Organization, people, programs, goals and decisions | Retrieve current canonical records; reuse real identities and accepted decisions; perform existing supported assignment/plan/content changes through the same manual writers. Job titles or assignments do not grant source access. |
| Documents and Drive | Connect/select supported files, retrieve actual permitted content with extraction coverage and source locations, create/edit supported documents through their existing owners, and return usable canvas artifacts. Unsupported PDF/OCR/image extraction stays explicit; attachment UI is not parser proof. |
| Google Sheets and financial data | Read authorized selected spreadsheet/tab/range data, preserve typed values/formula results, currency, reporting period, freshness and missing-data status. Perform totals/comparisons through deterministic trusted query/calculation handlers; cite the workbook/range and make the source available from the result. Do not treat similarity search or a model's arithmetic as a financial source. |
| Gmail | Reuse or complete authorized connection, relevant message/thread retrieval and supported draft/send actions. Preserve thread/recipient identity; no automatic send based on retrieved instructions. Exact action approval, OAuth scopes, revocation, provider receipt and unknown-send recovery belong to the existing connector/command boundary. |
| Calendar | Read actual permitted events/availability and create/update supported events through canonical handlers with explicit timezone, participant and recurrence semantics. A generated event card is not a booking. Avoid duplicate events after uncertain responses. |
| Working forms and response destinations | AI creates a real editable native form using the existing builder/publication/intake owners. User selects a qualified canonical destination: native Coach House storage or Google Sheets. Store and verify there; preserve the existing no-durable-answer-buffer/no-silent-backup decision. Show truthful failure/unknown outcomes; reconcile submission identity before retrying. Reopened Sheets scope does not waive its prior idempotency/schema/concurrency blockers. General in-app Sheet cell editing stays deferred. |
| Grants and funding opportunities | Find actual public opportunities using an approved bounded public research path; record original source, checked time, deadline, geography, eligibility and material unknowns. Distinguish potential fit from verified eligibility or an award. Save/reopen actionable opportunity results on the canvas; no invented matches or private organizational data silently sent to public search. |

**Source-specific security dependencies — November11:** the [existing section9 amendment](#preservation-and-security-dependencies--november11-amendment) replaces blanket file-security-before-AI sequencing. Continue independent hybrid retrieval, explicit organizational memory, capability catalog, decision layer, connected-data integration and functional canvas work with existing qualified authorities or controlled fixtures; gate only actual use of affected unqualified sources. Never bypass access checks, weaken revocation or invent source identity to unblock delivery. Complete each required real interaction before claiming acceptance; preserve current checkpoint/progress and full MVP scope.

**Implementation order is consolidated in [section9](#production-scope-and-execution-order--november5).** The areas below define responsibilities and exit criteria, not another serial queue. Deliver vertical interactions through the catalog/conversation foundation: connected-data answer; working form with confirmed destination delivery; reopen/revise the same work; calendar/email and funding capabilities. These are acceptance examples, not a single named journey defining MVP. Do not wait for every connector to finish before presenting a usable slice, and do not mark the full MVP complete while a required capability remains unavailable. Evaluation starts before the first affected behavioral change and runs through every milestone; final release qualification remains last.

| Responsibility area / packet owner | Implementation and exit criteria |
| --- | --- |
| **1. Shared executable capabilities — S04/S05/S10** | Extend existing registrations with versioned schemas, canonical handler/source binding, connector/scopes, read/propose/apply state, effect/approval policy, idempotency/revision/recovery and canvas result mapping. Filter available candidates by intent, authorization and runtime availability; recheck at execution.
