**Continuous evaluation, from the beginning:** use existing cases and receipts to establish a small baseline before changing affected behavior; no large new evaluation platform blocks delivery. Add deterministic regression cases alongside implementation. For relevant prompt/model/tool/retrieval/configuration changes, run appropriately scoped real-provider comparisons only under explicit budget/data authorization. Version the case manifest, exact model/prompt/schema/index configuration and expected invariants; separate tuning from held-out qualification. Measure first-attempt usefulness, grounded claims, tool choice, preserved work, actual task completion, latency stages and all costs/attempts. Freeze capability-specific thresholds before candidate comparison; code graders check permissions/state/math and calibrated human review assesses usefulness. Safety failures cannot be averaged away. Existing tests are not proof of provider quality or deployment.

**Evidence examples:** (a) a board member asks about a linked financial Sheet and receives reproducible figures with period/range and current access; (b) a plan includes a working volunteer form, a real share path, and a submission confirmed at its selected destination; (c) a new chat uses saved organizational guidance, then respects its correction/deletion; (d) a saved plan/document is revised without duplicate artifacts or overwritten collaborator work; (e) a funding question returns real cited opportunities with eligibility uncertainty; (f) authorized email/calendar actions produce actual receipts, while denied/revoked scopes disclose nothing. Test varied organizations and objectives, sparse/conflicting data and interruptions. A successful screenshot or mock is not end-to-end proof.

**Accounting, privacy and recovery remain shared:** existing SQL reservations, member/org caps, concurrency/hourly limits, finite request/loop bounds, immutable receipts and uncertain-cost recovery remain authoritative. Include embedding/indexing and decision calls in provider exposure, finite job/run budgets and operation tracing; explicitly decide whether background index expense is platform expense or an approved customer charge before enabling billing. Do not hide new paid work in existing generation quotes. Trace permitted IDs/status/duration, evidence revisions, validation, application and cost certainty without dumping source bodies, secrets or hidden reasoning. A disconnect never starts another paid run automatically; Stop prevents new dispatch while already incurred cost is reconciled. Generation-disabled states still permit authorized recovery. Chat deletion preserves accepted board records and required accounting; source-derived indexes/guidance obey their own deletion/access policy. Do not reintroduce deferred independent historical-restore infrastructure as an incidental dependency.

**Documentation qualification:** implement against primary documentation for the exact installed/selected versions and configured provider identities, not generic examples or claims of “2026” readiness. AI SDK documents [message persistence](https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/ai-sdk-ui/chatbot-message-persistence), [typed/transient data](https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/ai-sdk-ui/streaming-data) and [stream recovery/stop](https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/ai-sdk-ui/chatbot-resume-streams); Supabase documents [hybrid search](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai/hybrid-search); [OpenAI Decisions](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/decisions) and [Jev integration](https://vercel.com/i/jev-agent-control) describe bounded judgment distinct from execution authority. Confirm actual Google API/account scopes and provider guarantees at each integration. OpenAI [data controls](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data) distinguish `store:false` from account-wide zero retention. Documentation availability is not enabled access or product acceptance.

**Deferred sophistication, not essential capability:** automatic memory extraction/autonomous memory management, advanced reranking, dynamic tool discovery, automatic model fallback, workflow-engine replacement, sub-agents, skill-loading infrastructure, general bidirectional sync/arbitrary Sheet editing, individual-result dragging and coach handoff remain separately scoped. Tool-selection efficiency, explicit guidance, semantic retrieval and bounded decision support are required now. Do not build every item in the110-feature future catalog. Existing pricing/Stripe commercial qualification remains separate; nothing here activates sales or provider allowances.

Follow the current fresh-chat checkpoint and [section9 active execution order](#production-scope-and-execution-order--november5), including its source-specific security dependencies; do not restart completed capability/conversation work. Guidance joins connected-data delivery. The responsibility areas above retain their detailed contracts. #### Team credits, multiple chats and minimal payment flow — November4

Extends P3/D6 and S05 accounting; this is planned product behavior, not a claim that personal funding or live credit sales are enabled. Unlimited team seats do not imply unlimited AI spending. Preserve the existing sidebar usage entry and Account settings > Usage & billing; do not create another billing surface in each chat.

**Existing foundation verified in source:** organization wallet, owner-only credit purchases, organization/member monthly caps, atomic maximum-cost reservation, idempotent settlement and signed-webhook purchase fulfillment. Current admission permits one unsettled request per actor across chats and an independently configured organization concurrency ceiling. Concurrent requests cannot spend the same reserved credits. Blank member limits currently mean no owner-imposed cap, not a funded allocation. Source inspection does not establish current hosted configuration.

**Team-funded first slice:**

- Keep one organization pool across its workspaces/chats. Each request records its authenticated actor and organization; each person's chats aggregate against the same member limit. A new thread, tab, seat or workspace does not create credits or reset usage. Thread identity and conversation visibility remain separate from billing identity.
- Owners set a default monthly budget for new members and individual overrides, including zero for AI off. Do not silently assign a numerical commercial default or retroactively pause existing users; settle that policy before rollout. Pending invites may carry an intended limit but cannot spend until accepted membership is verified. Role permissions still govern AI eligibility.
- A cap is permission to consume the shared pool, not credits reserved for that person. Show shared funds separately; do not promise that every member's remaining cap is funded. Monthly cap reset does not replenish or extend purchased/included credit lots. If earmarked guaranteed balances are desired later, they require explicit allocation/reclaim accounting, not relabeling caps.
- In the existing team management view, use compact avatar/name rows with a thin usage bar, used/limit and distinguishable in-flight reservation. Keep detailed history and explanations on demand. No invented progress percentage for an uncapped member; accessible text must convey usage without relying on color. Members see their own budget; owners can manage team budgets under server authorization.
- Preserve chats, drafts, manual canvas tools and previous results when funds or limits run out. Block only new paid generation, with one relevant recovery action. A funded owner can adjust a member limit; an empty pool requires purchasing credits. Proposed member action is Request credits, routed to the owner with duplicate suppression and honest delivered/pending state; do not ship a dead button or introduce an unrequested messaging integration.

**Minimal UI/payment contract:** one primary button for the current task, one clearly named action per button. In usage, Buy credits opens a compact selection with the amount, credits and funding destination visible, then one Pay action hands off to hosted Stripe Checkout. Use the configured catalog; do not invent pack prices. No redundant confirmation chain, dense billing dashboard, automatic recharge enrollment or manual activation step. Adjust limit changes permission only and must never imply a purchase. An optional team-member purchase shortcut must disclose both the team-pool destination and any proposed cap change; do not conflate them or ship it before atomic/recoverable behavior is defined. Keep the default team-budget slice simple.

**Personal funding is a separate follow-up, not a prerequisite for chat:** members may eventually buy their own credits through the same simple checkout, with a clearly selected funding source (Team or Personal), scoped ownership, reservations and receipts. No silent fallback from team funds to personal funds, no charge to another member and no bypass of workspace permissions or provider safety ceilings. Personal wallets, member purchase authorization, refund handling and credit ownership on team removal must be defined and verified before exposing this option. Existing purchases are organization-owner-only.

**Stripe setup and activation:** reuse Coach House's existing merchant integration. Verify live account payment readiness, matching live keys/webhook signing secret, deployed purchase/accounting migrations and handlers, enabled catalog packs bound to the correct Stripe one-time Prices, return URLs and approved pricing/refund/allowance policy. AI policy/wallet availability and `WORKSPACE_AI_PURCHASES_ENABLED` are additional application gates; a paid balance does not bypass service limits. Do not enable sales until test-mode checkout, cancellation, confirmed payment, replay, delayed webhook, refund restrictions and fresh balance readback pass, followed by required hosted quality/release checks and separately authorized live verification. No configuration, purchase or deployment is authorized by this documentation update.

After verified successful payment, the existing signed-webhook path should grant the purchased credits exactly once and refresh usage automatically. Returning from Checkout or seeing a success page is not proof of payment. If verification is pending, show a concise pending state and reconcile the same order; never ask the customer to pay again to activate it. No routine manual activation by Coach House. Reference: [Stripe Checkout fulfillment](https://docs.stripe.com/checkout/fulfillment) and [Stripe account activation](https://support.stripe.com/topics/getting-started).

**Acceptance:** simultaneous users and separate chats cannot overspend the wallet or member caps; repeat submissions/payment events cannot duplicate debits or grants; source/account switches and membership revocation are enforced server-side. Verify funded versus exhausted pool, zero/capped/uncapped member, month boundary with in-flight reservations, accepted invite/default budget, payment pending/recovery and compact keyboard/mobile flows. Record live activation as a separate gate, not inferred from source or UI tests.
